A conventional post-training quantization approach applied to networks with decomposed weights yields a drop in accuracy. Therefore, our goal is to develop an algorithm that finds tensor approximation directly with quantized factors and thus benefit from both compression techniques while keeping the prediction quality of the model. Namely, we propose to use Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) for approximating a float tensor by a tensor of Canonical Polyadic format (CP), whose factors are close to their quantized versions. This leads to lower approximation error after quantization and smaller quality drop in model predictions while maintaining the same compression rate.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a novel approach to neural network compression that performs tensor factorization and quantization simultaneously.
standard_prompt: The study introduces ADMM-based CP factorization for deep neural network compression, achieving better accuracy retention during quantization compared to traditional approaches, offering a balance between reduced parameter count and maintained performance on constrained devices.
cot_prompt: Our work proposes using ADMM for approximating float tensors via CP factorization, achieving lower quantization errors and minimal prediction loss compared to traditional post-training methods.
dsp_prompt: Our novel ADMM-based method accurately approximates float tensors using CP factorizations, reducing parameter counts and improving model accuracy during post-decomposition quantization while achieving comparable compression rates with minimal loss in predictive performance.

titles: Sobolev GAN
keywords: GAN theory; Integral Probability Metrics; elliptic PDE and diffusion; GAN for discrete sequences; semi-supervised learning.
abstracts: We propose a new Integral Probability Metric (IPM) between distributions: the Sobolev IPM. The Sobolev IPM compares the mean discrepancy of two distributions for functions (critic) restricted to a Sobolev ball defined with respect to a dominant measure mu. We show that the Sobolev IPM compares two distributions in high dimensions based on weighted conditional Cumulative Distribution Functions (CDF) of each coordinate on a leave one out basis. The Dominant measure mu plays a crucial role as it defines the support on which conditional CDFs are compared. Sobolev IPM can be seen as an extension of the one dimensional Von-Mises Cramer statistics to high dimensional distributions. We show how Sobolev IPM can be used to train Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). We then exploit the intrinsic conditioning implied by Sobolev IPM in text generation. Finally we show that a variant of Sobolev GAN achieves competitive results in semi-supervised learning on CIFAR-10, thanks to the smoothness enforced on the critic by Sobolev GAN which relates to Laplacian regularization.
one_sentence_summary: We define a new Integral Probability Metric (Sobolev IPM) and show how it can be used for training GANs for text generation and semi-supervised learning.
standard_prompt: We introduce the Sobolev Integral Probability Metric, extending Von-Mises Cramér statistics to high-dimensional distributions through conditional cumulative distribution functions, demonstrating its application in training Generative Adversarial Networks and achieving competitive performance in semi-supervised learning tasks.
cot_prompt: We introduce the Sobolev Integral Probability Metric, a novel distance measure for comparing distributions, particularly useful for training Generative Adversarial Networks and leveraging their properties for tasks like text generation and semi-supervised learning.
dsp_prompt: We introduce the Sobolev Integral Probability Metric (Sobolev IPM), a novel tool for comparing distributions in high dimensions using the Mean Discrepancy principle, specifically designed for training Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) through its application in text generation and achieving competitive performance in semi-supervised learning tasks like CIFAR-10 classification.

titles: Demystifying Batch Normalization in ReLU Networks: Equivalent Convex Optimization Models and Implicit Regularization
keywords: batch normalization; ReLU networks; deep networks; convex optimization; whitening; implicit regularization; algorithmic bias
abstracts: Batch Normalization (BN) is a commonly used technique to accelerate and stabilize training of deep neural networks. Despite its empirical success, a full theoretical understanding of BN is yet to be developed. In this work, we analyze BN through the lens of convex optimization. We introduce an analytic framework based on convex duality to obtain exact convex representations of weight-decay regularized ReLU networks with BN, which can be trained in polynomial-time. Our analyses also show that optimal layer weights can be obtained as simple closed-form formulas in the high-dimensional and/or overparameterized regimes. Furthermore, we find that Gradient Descent provides an algorithmic bias effect on the standard non-convex BN network, and we design an approach to explicitly encode this implicit regularization into the convex objective. Experiments with CIFAR image classification highlight the effectiveness of this explicit regularization for mimicking and substantially improving the performance of standard BN networks.
one_sentence_summary: We introduce an analytic framework based on convex duality to obtain exact and polynomial-time trainable convex representations of weight-decay regularized ReLU networks with BN.
standard_prompt: Through novel convex optimization frameworks, including equivalent models and gradient descent algorithms, researchers demonstrate how Batch Normalization (BN) can be analyzed and optimized, revealing both computational efficiency gains and improved generalization properties in deep learning tasks.
cot_prompt: Batch normalization's performance gains are attributed to equivalent convex optimization models and explicit regularization via gradient descent, revealing an algorithmic bias effect that enhances standard techniques like batch normalization in deep learning.
dsp_prompt: Through an analytical framework based on convex duality, this study reveals exact convex formulations of weight-decay regularized ReLU networks with Batch Normalization, providing polynomial-time training algorithms and finding optimal layer weights via closed-form solutions in specific regimes, while demonstrating that gradient descent introduces an algorithmic bias effect, leading to improved performance through explicit regularization.

titles: Minimum Description Length Control
keywords: multitask reinforcement learning; RL; reinforcement learning; MDL
abstracts: We propose a novel framework for multitask reinforcement learning based on the minimum description length (MDL) principle. In this approach, which we term MDL-control (MDL-C), the agent learns the common structure among the tasks with which it is faced and then distills it into a simpler representation which facilitates faster convergence and generalization to new tasks. In doing so, MDL-C naturally balances adaptation to each task with epistemic uncertainty about the task distribution. We motivate MDL-C via formal connections between the MDL principle and Bayesian inference, derive theoretical performance guarantees, and demonstrate MDL-C's empirical effectiveness on both discrete and high-dimensional continuous control tasks.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a novel framework for multitask reinforcement learning which seeks to distill shared structure among tasks into a low-complexity representation, which is then leveraged to accelerate convergence on new tasks.
standard_prompt: We introduce MDL-control (MDL-C), a novel framework for multitask reinforcement learning that combines the minimum description length (MDL) principle with Bayesian inference to learn shared structures across tasks while balancing adaptation and epistemic uncertainty, leading to improved convergence and generalization.
cot_prompt: We introduce MDL-Control (MDL-C), a novel multitask reinforcement learning framework that leverages the minimum description length principle to learn shared structures across tasks, enabling faster convergence and better generalization through simplified representations.
dsp_prompt: In this work, we introduce MDL-Control, a method that combines the Minimum Description Length principle with reinforcement learning to learn shared structures across multiple tasks, thereby enhancing adaptability and reducing computational complexity.

titles: Powderworld: A Platform for Understanding Generalization via Rich Task Distributions
keywords: reinforcement learning; environment; generalization; out-of-distribution; multi-task
abstracts: One of the grand challenges of reinforcement learning is the ability to generalize to new tasks. However, general agents require a set of rich, diverse tasks to train on. Designing a `foundation environment' for such tasks is tricky -- the ideal environment would support a range of emergent phenomena, an expressive task space, and fast runtime. To take a step towards addressing this research bottleneck, this work presents Powderworld, a lightweight yet expressive simulation environment running directly on the GPU. Within Powderworld, two motivating task distributions are presented, one for world-modelling and one for reinforcement learning. Each contains hand-designed test tasks to examine generalization. Experiments indicate that increasing the environment's complexity improves generalization for world models, yet causes reinforcement learning agents to struggle. Powderworld aims to support the study of generalization by providing a source of diverse tasks arising from the same core rules.
one_sentence_summary: Powderworld is an environment supporting the study of generalization by providing diverse tasks arising from the same core rules.
standard_prompt: Powderworld is a lightweight yet expressive simulation environment designed to support the study of generalization through its diverse task distributions, which improve performance in world modeling but challenge reinforcement learning agents.
cot_prompt: Powderworld, a GPU-based simulation environment, supports diverse task distributions for studying generalization across different reinforcement learning paradigms, demonstrating improved performance in world modeling but challenging reinforcement learning agents.
dsp_prompt: Powderworld, a GPU-accelerated simulation platform designed to facilitate exploration of generalization through rich, diverse task distributions, showcases its potential for improving both world-modeling and reinforcement-learning agent performance.

titles: Mix-review: Alleviate Forgetting in the Pretrain-Finetune Framework for Neural Language Generation Models
keywords: language generation; forgetting; pretraining; open-domain dialogue
abstracts: In this work, we study how the large-scale pretrain-finetune framework changes the behavior of a neural language generator. We focus on the transformer encoder-decoder model for the open-domain dialogue response generation task. We find that after standard fine-tuning, the model forgets important language generation skills acquired during large-scale pre-training. We demonstrate the forgetting phenomenon through a detailed behavior analysis from the perspectives of context sensitivity and knowledge transfer. Adopting the concept of data mixing, we propose an intuitive fine-tuning strategy named "mix-review''. We find that mix-review effectively regularize the fine-tuning process, and the forgetting problem is largely alleviated. Finally, we discuss interesting behavior of the resulting dialogue model and its implications.
one_sentence_summary: We identify the forgetting problem in fine-tuning of pre-trained NLG models, and propose the mix-review strategy to address it.
standard_prompt: The study examines the forgetting issue in a neural language generation model's pretrain-finetune framework, finding it exacerbated by standard fine-tuning, which results in significant performance degradation. Introducing a novel "mix-review" fine-tuning method significantly reduces forgetting and improves model performance through data mixing, leading to better contextual and knowledge-transfer capabilities.
cot_prompt: The study explores the forgetting issue in a transformer-based neural language generator using the pretrain-finetune framework, finding that mix-review fine-tuning improves learning by integrating pre-trained knowledge with domain-specific tasks.
dsp_prompt: The traditional pretrain-finetune approach leads to significant forgetting in neural language generators, which can be mitigated using a novel "mix-review" fine-tuning method.

titles: Zero-Mean Regularized Spectral Contrastive Learning: Implicitly Mitigating Wrong Connections in Positive-Pair Graphs
keywords: Contrastive Learning; Unsupervised Domain Adaptation; Learning with Noisy Labels
abstracts: Contrastive learning has emerged as a popular paradigm of self-supervised learning that learns representations by encouraging representations of positive pairs to be similar while representations of negative pairs to be far apart. The spectral contrastive loss, in synergy with the notion of positive-pair graphs, offers valuable theoretical insights into the empirical successes of contrastive learning. In this paper, we propose incorporating an additive factor into the term of spectral contrastive loss involving negative pairs. This simple modification can be equivalently viewed as introducing a regularization term that enforces the mean of representations to be zero, which thus is referred to as *zero-mean regularization*. It intuitively relaxes the orthogonality of representations between negative pairs and implicitly alleviates the adverse effect of wrong connections in the positive-pair graph, leading to better performance and robustness. To clarify this, we thoroughly investigate the role of zero-mean regularized spectral contrastive loss in both unsupervised and supervised scenarios with respect to theoretical analysis and quantitative evaluation. These results highlight the potential of zero-mean regularized spectral contrastive learning to be a promising approach in various tasks.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a theoretically sound and effective approach for mitigating wrong connections in spectral contrastive learning with positive-pair graphs .
standard_prompt: The authors introduce zero-mean regularized spectral contrastive learning, proposing a simple modification to the spectral contrastive loss that effectively mitigates wrong connections in positive-pair graphs through zero-mean regularization, enhancing representation similarity and overall performance across different scenarios.
cot_prompt: Zero-mean regularization introduces an implicit regularization term into the spectral contrastive loss function, helping to alleviate incorrect connections within positive-pair graphs and improve representation alignment for better performance across different types of training scenarios.
dsp_prompt: In this paper, we introduce a novel zero-mean regularization term to the spectral contrastive loss function to improve representation quality and robustness in both unsupervised and supervised settings through theoretical analysis and empirical evaluations.

titles: Improved Estimation of Concentration Under $\ell_p$-Norm Distance Metrics Using Half Spaces
keywords: Adversarial Examples; Concentration of Measure; Gaussian Isoperimetric Inequality
abstracts: Concentration of measure has been argued to be the fundamental cause of adversarial vulnerability. Mahloujifar et al. (2019) presented an empirical way to measure the concentration of a data distribution using samples, and employed it to find lower bounds on intrinsic robustness for several benchmark datasets. However, it remains unclear whether these lower bounds are tight enough to provide a useful approximation for the intrinsic robustness of a dataset. To gain a deeper understanding of the concentration of measure phenomenon, we first extend the Gaussian Isoperimetric Inequality to non-spherical Gaussian measures and arbitrary $\ell_p$-norms ($p \geq 2$). We leverage these theoretical insights to design a method that uses half-spaces to estimate the concentration of any empirical dataset under $\ell_p$-norm distance metrics. Our proposed algorithm is more efficient than Mahloujifar et al. (2019)'s, and experiments on synthetic datasets and image benchmarks demonstrate that it is able to find much tighter intrinsic robustness bounds. These tighter estimates provide further evidence that rules out intrinsic dataset concentration as a possible explanation for the adversarial vulnerability of state-of-the-art classifiers.
one_sentence_summary: We show that concentration of measure does not prohibit the existence of adversarially robust classifiers using a novel method of empirical concentration estimation.
standard_prompt: By extending the Gaussian Isoperimetric Inequality to arbitrary $\ell_p$-norms and leveraging half-spaces, our study introduces a more efficient method for estimating concentration of measure under $\ell_p$-norm distances, demonstrating improved accuracy over previous approaches through both synthetic and real-world datasets.
cot_prompt: We develop a novel estimator using half-spaces to improve the estimation of concentration under $\ell_p$-norm distances, showing significant efficiency gains over existing methods and providing tighter bounds on intrinsic robustness, thus challenging the notion that concentration causes adversarial vulnerability.
dsp_prompt: We extend the Gaussian Isoperimetric Inequality to non-spherical Gaussian measures with arbitrary $\ell_p$-norms and develop a novel method using half-spaces to efficiently estimate the concentration of empirical datasets under $\ell_p$-norm distance metrics, offering improved bounds over existing approaches like Mahloujifar et al.'s work.

titles: Diversity-Sensitive Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks
keywords: Conditional Generative Adversarial Network; mode-collapse; multi-modal generation; image-to-image translation; image in-painting; video prediction
abstracts: We propose a simple yet highly effective method that addresses the mode-collapse problem in the Conditional Generative  Adversarial  Network (cGAN). Although conditional distributions are multi-modal (i.e., having many modes) in practice, most cGAN approaches tend to learn an overly simplified distribution where an input is always mapped to a single output regardless of variations in latent code. To address such issue, we propose to explicitly regularize the generator to produce diverse outputs depending on latent codes. The proposed regularization is simple, general, and can be easily integrated into most conditional GAN objectives. Additionally, explicit regularization on generator allows our method to control a balance between visual quality and diversity. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on three conditional generation tasks: image-to-image translation, image inpainting, and future video prediction. We show that simple addition of our regularization to existing models leads to surprisingly diverse generations, substantially outperforming the previous approaches for multi-modal conditional generation specifically designed in each individual task.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a simple and general approach that avoids a mode collapse problem in various conditional GANs.
standard_prompt: We introduce a simple yet effective regularization technique for Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (cGANs), addressing the issue of over-simplification by generating diverse outputs across multiple modalities through explicit regularization, demonstrating superior performance in image-to-image translation, image inpainting, and future video prediction tasks compared to traditional methods.
cot_prompt: Our method introduces a simple yet effective way to prevent conditioning-based conditional generative adversarial networks from learning overly simplistic distributions by explicitly regularizing the generator to produce diverse outputs, demonstrating improved performance across various tasks compared to traditional methods.
dsp_prompt: Our method introduces explicit regularization to improve the diversity of generated outputs in Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks by controlling the balance between visual quality and generality across multiple modalities, demonstrating superior performance over traditional approaches in tasks like image-to-image translation, image inpainting, and future video prediction.

titles: How (Un)Fair is Text Summarization?
keywords: Natural language processing; Summarization; Fairness
abstracts: Creating a good summary requires carefully choosing details from the original text to accurately represent it in a limited space. If a summary contains biased information about a group, it risks passing this bias off to readers as fact. These risks increase if we consider not just one biased summary, but rather a biased summarization algorithm. Despite this, little work has measured whether these summarizers demonstrate biased performance. Rather, most work in summarization focuses on improving performance, ignoring questions of bias. In this paper we demonstrate that automatic summarizers both amplify and introduce bias towards information about under-represented groups. Additionally, we show that summarizers are highly sensitive to document structure, making the summaries they generate unstable under changes that are semantically meaningless to humans, which poses a further fairness risk. Given these results, and the large scale potential for harm presented by biased summarization, we recommend that bias analysis be performed and reported on summarizers to ensure that new automatic summarization methods do not introduce bias to the summaries they generate.
one_sentence_summary: We show that machine learning based summarizers exhibit bias toward different groups and are very sensitive to document structure.
standard_prompt: Automatic text summarization algorithms often inadvertently promote and perpetuate biases against underrepresented groups due to their reliance on document structure and the amplification of existing biases, highlighting the need for transparent bias analysis before deploying such systems.
cot_prompt: Text summarization algorithms can inadvertently amplify biases present in their training data, potentially leading to misleading or unfair representations of diverse groups.
dsp_prompt: Automatic summarization algorithms often amplify biases present in their training data, especially when dealing with underrepresented groups, potentially leading to inaccurate and misleading summaries due to inherent structural sensitivities.

titles: HiLLoC: lossless image compression with hierarchical latent variable models
keywords: compression; variational inference; lossless compression; deep latent variable models
abstracts: We make the following striking observation: fully convolutional VAE models trained on 32x32 ImageNet can generalize well, not just to 64x64 but also to far larger photographs, with no changes to the model. We use this property, applying fully convolutional models to lossless compression, demonstrating a method to scale the VAE-based 'Bits-Back with ANS' algorithm for lossless compression to large color photographs, and achieving state of the art for compression of full size ImageNet images. We release Craystack, an open source library for convenient prototyping of lossless compression using probabilistic models, along with full implementations of all of our compression results.
one_sentence_summary: We scale up lossless compression with latent variables, achieving state of the art on full-size ImageNet images.
standard_prompt: The authors demonstrate that fully convolutional Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) trained on small datasets can be effectively applied to lossless compression, achieving state-of-the-art performance on large color photographs by scaling up existing algorithms like "Bits-Back with ANS."
cot_prompt: We demonstrate that fully convolutional variational autoencoders trained on ImageNet achieve remarkable generalization capabilities, enabling efficient lossless compression of full-size color photographs by leveraging probabilistic models through the Craystack library.
dsp_prompt: The authors leverage fully convolutional Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) trained on ImageNet to develop a lossless image compression technique called "HiLLoC," which they apply to compress large color photographs up to full-size ImageNet images, achieving superior performance compared to previous methods.

titles: A Johnson-Lindenstrauss Framework for Randomly Initialized CNNs
keywords: convolutional neural networks; Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma; initialization; isometry; theory.
abstracts: How does the geometric representation of a dataset change after the application of each randomly initialized layer of a neural network? The celebrated Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma answers this question for linear fully-connected neural networks (FNNs), stating that the geometry is essentially preserved. For FNNs with the ReLU activation, the angle between two input contracts according to a known mapping. The question for non-linear convolutional neural networks (CNNs) becomes much more intricate. To answer this question, we introduce a geometric framework. For linear CNNs, we show that the Johnson--Lindenstrauss lemma continues to hold, namely, that the angle between two inputs is preserved. For CNNs with ReLU activation, on the other hand, the behavior is richer: The angle between the outputs contracts, where the level of contraction depends on the nature of the inputs. In particular, after one layer, the geometry of natural images is essentially preserved, whereas for Gaussian correlated inputs, CNNs exhibit the same contracting behavior as FNNs with ReLU activation.
one_sentence_summary: We study how the geometric representation of a dataset change after the application of each randomly initialized layer of a neural network.
standard_prompt: The study explores how geometric properties of data change through layers of randomly initialized convolutional neural networks (CNNs), focusing on the preservation of angles using the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma but finding varying levels of distortion depending on the type of inputs.
cot_prompt: The study explores how geometric properties of data change through layers of CNNs, finding that while linear CNNs maintain their geometry, nonlinear ones contract angles between outputs depending on the input's distribution.
dsp_prompt: The Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma holds for linear convolutional neural networks but exhibits rich behavior for CNNs with ReLU activation, leading to varying levels of geometry preservation depending on the input distribution.

titles: Bi-linear Value Networks for Multi-goal Reinforcement Learning
keywords: Multi-goal reinforcement learning; universal value function approximator
abstracts:
Universal value functions are a core component of off-policy multi-goal reinforcement learning. 
The de-facto paradigm is to approximate Q(s, a, g) using monolithic neural networks which lack inductive biases to produce complex interactions between the state s and the goal g. In this work, we propose a bilinear decomposition that represents the Q-value via a low-rank approximation in the form of a dot product between two vector fields. The first vector field, f(s, a), captures the environment's local dynamics at the state s; whereas the second component, ϕ(s, g), captures the global relationship between the current state and the goal.
We show that our bilinear decomposition scheme improves sample efficiency over the original monolithic value approximators, and transfer better to unseen goals. We demonstrate significant learning speed-up over a variety of tasks on a simulated robot arm, and the challenging task of dexterous manipulation with a Shadow hand.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a bilinear value function for multi-goal reinforcement learning and show superior sample efficiency and generalizability.
standard_prompt: A novel bilinear decomposition approach, represented by a low-rank approximation involving two vector fields, significantly enhances sample efficiency and generalizes across diverse goals in multi-goal reinforcement learning, outperforming traditional monolithic methods on simulated robotic tasks and dexterous manipulation challenges.
cot_prompt: Our bilinear decomposition method enhances sample efficiency in off-policy multi-goal reinforcement learning by representing Q-values through a low-rank dot product between two vector fields, capturing both local and global state-goal relationships. This approach leads to faster learning speeds and improved performance across various tasks including robotic manipulation.
dsp_prompt: In this work, we introduce a bilinear decomposition of the Q-function to improve sample efficiency and adaptability in off-policy multi-goal reinforcement learning, showcasing benefits across various domains including robotics.

titles: Adaptive Offline Data Replay in Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning
keywords: offline-to-online reinforcement learning; offline data replay
abstracts: Offline-to-online reinforcement learning allows agents to benefit from both sample efficiency and performance by integrating offline and online learning stages. One central challenge in this setting is how to effectively combine the rich experiences collected offline with real-time online explorations. Previous works commonly adopted predetermined mixing ratios for offline data replay as a primary approach to harness offline data in online training. However, determining the best mixing ratio that suits a specific environment and offline dataset often demands empirical adjustments that are context-specific. To address this, we propose a new approach for offline data replay that dynamically adjusts the mixing ratio based on the exploration reward of the agent in the online learning phase. Specifically, our method employs a bandit model to explore and exploit various mixing ratios, subsequently establishing a dynamic adjustment pattern for these ratios to enhance offline data utilization. Empirical results demonstrate that our approach outperforms conventional offline data replay methods, consistently proving its effectiveness across various environments and datasets without the need for targeted, context-specific adjustments.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a method to adaptively leverage offline data in the online training of offline-to-online reinforcement learning.
standard_prompt: Our proposed adaptive offline data replay strategy dynamically adjusts mixing ratios using a bandit model, enhancing offline data utilization through dynamic exploration and exploitation, achieving superior performance compared to traditional approaches in diverse environments and datasets.
cot_prompt: Our study proposes a novel adaptive offline data replay strategy that dynamically adjusts mixing ratios based on exploration rewards, significantly enhancing offline data's utility in online reinforcement learning settings.
dsp_prompt: In offline-to-online reinforcement learning, dynamically adjusting the mixing ratio between offline and online data using a bandit model improves performance by optimizing the balance of experience and exploration across different environments and datasets.

titles: Efficient Riemannian Optimization on the Stiefel Manifold via the Cayley Transform
keywords: Orthonormality; Efficient Riemannian Optimization; the Stiefel manifold.
abstracts: Strictly enforcing orthonormality constraints on parameter matrices has been shown advantageous in deep learning. This amounts to Riemannian optimization on the Stiefel manifold, which, however, is computationally expensive. To address this challenge, we present two main contributions: (1) A new efficient retraction map based on an iterative Cayley transform for optimization updates, and (2) An implicit vector transport mechanism based on the combination of a projection of the momentum and the Cayley transform on the Stiefel manifold. We specify two new optimization algorithms: Cayley SGD with momentum, and Cayley ADAM on the Stiefel manifold. Convergence of Cayley SGD is theoretically analyzed. Our experiments for CNN training demonstrate that both algorithms: (a) Use less running time per iteration relative to existing approaches that enforce orthonormality of CNN parameters; and (b) Achieve faster convergence rates than the baseline SGD and ADAM algorithms without compromising the performance of the CNN. Cayley SGD and Cayley ADAM are also shown to reduce the training time for optimizing the unitary transition matrices in RNNs.
one_sentence_summary: This paper is about efficient Riemannian optimization on the Stiefel manifold that enforces the parameter matrices orthonormal.
standard_prompt: The authors introduce efficient optimization methods on the Stiefel manifold using the Cayley transform, achieving significant speed improvements over traditional orthonormalization techniques while maintaining competitive convergence rates in deep learning applications.
cot_prompt: The authors introduce efficient optimization methods on the Stiefel manifold using the Cayley transform, achieving reduced computational costs and improved convergence rates compared to traditional approaches.
dsp_prompt: The authors introduce two efficient optimization methods for Riemannian problems on the Stiefel manifold using the Cayley transform, achieving significant computational savings while maintaining competitive performance in tasks such as image classification and recurrent neural network parameter optimization.

titles: Learning Diverse and Effective Policies with Non-Markovian Rewards
keywords: policy diversity; non-Markovian Rewards; reinforcement learning
abstracts: Learning a set of diverse and high-quantity policies is a difficult problem in Reinforcement Learning since the diversity of policies is demanded to be achieved without dampening their effectiveness. This problem becomes more challenging when the rewards are non-Markovian, i.e., the rewards depend on the history of states and actions, which are quite sparse and returned over a long period. The sparse supervision signals and the non-Markovian properties of the rewards hinder the learning of policy embeddings and thus the learning of diverse and high-quality policies. In this paper, we propose to use a diversity matrix to quantify policy diversity and theoretically prove that if the diversity matrix is positive definite, then the diversity of policies can be achieved without sacrificing their effectiveness. The policy diversity matrix stems from policy embeddings. To obtain high-quality embeddings, we adopt a transformer to capture mutual dependencies between states and actions and design pseudo tasks to overcome sparse rewards. Experimental results show that our method can achieve a set of policies with more effective diversity and better performance than multiple recently proposed baseline methods in a variety of non-Markovian and Markovian environments.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a diversity matrix to quantify policy diversity and theoretically prove that if the diversity matrix is positive definite, then the diversity of policies can be achieved without sacrificing their effectiveness.
standard_prompt: The authors introduce a novel approach using a diversity matrix derived from policy embeddings to address the challenge of achieving diverse yet effective policies in reinforcement learning, especially in non-Markovian reward scenarios, by leveraging transformers for capturing state-action dependencies and designing pseudo tasks to surmount sparse reward issues.
cot_prompt: Our method leverages policy embeddings and transformers to effectively learn diverse and high-quality policies despite non-Markovian rewards, achieving superior diversity compared to existing approaches in various reinforcement learning scenarios.
dsp_prompt: Learning diverse and effective policies in non-Markovian environments remains challenging due to the need for achieving high-diversity solutions while preserving policy effectiveness, particularly when dealing with sparse reward signals. A novel approach using transformer-based policy embeddings and pseudo tasks addresses these issues by proving theoretical conditions under which diversity can be maximized without compromising policy quality, enabling superior performance compared to existing techniques across both Markovian and non-Markovian scenarios.

titles: Compressing LLMs: The Truth is Rarely Pure and Never Simple
keywords: Compression; Large Language Models; Pruning; Quantization
abstracts: Despite their remarkable achievements, modern Large Language Models (LLMs) encounter exorbitant computational and memory footprints. Recently, several works have shown significant success in *training-free* and  *data-free* compression (pruning and quantization) of LLMs achieving 50-60\% sparsity and reducing the bit-width down to 3 or 4 bits per weight, with negligible perplexity degradation over the uncompressed baseline. As recent research efforts are focused on developing increasingly sophisticated compression methods, our work takes a step back, and re-evaluates the effectiveness of existing SoTA compression methods, which rely on a fairly simple and widely questioned metric, perplexity (even for dense LLMs). We introduce **K**nowledge-**I**ntensive **C**ompressed LLM Benchmar**K** **(LLM-KICK)**, a collection of carefully-curated tasks to re-define the evaluation protocol for compressed LLMs, which have significant alignment with their dense counterparts, and perplexity fail to capture subtle change in their true capabilities. LLM-KICK unveils many favorable merits and unfortunate plights of current SoTA compression methods: all pruning methods suffer significant performance degradation, sometimes at trivial sparsity ratios (*e.g.*, 25-30\%), and fail for N:M sparsity on knowledge-intensive tasks; current quantization methods are more successful than pruning; yet, pruned LLMs even at $\geq 50$\% sparsity are robust in-context retrieval and summarization systems; among others. LLM-KICK is designed to holistically access compressed LLMs' ability for language understanding, reasoning, generation, in-context retrieval, in-context summarization, *etc.* We hope our study can foster the development of better LLM compression methods. The reproduced codes are available at https://github.com/VITA-Group/llm-kick.
one_sentence_summary: We developed LLM-KICK to holistically access compressed LLMs’ ability for language understanding, reasoning, generation, in-context retrieval, long-context summarization, etc.
standard_prompt: Knowledge-Intensive Compressed Large Language Model Benchmarking (LLM-KICK) evaluates the capabilities of compressed models through diverse tasks that highlight their strengths and weaknesses compared to traditional measures like perplexity, revealing significant limitations in current compression techniques such as pruning and quantization across various applications including in-context retrieval and summarization.
cot_prompt: Our KICK framework reveals perplexity's limitations when evaluating compressed large language models, highlighting the diverse strengths and weaknesses across different compression techniques including pruning, quantization, and the necessity of considering domain-specific metrics like knowledge-independence and context-awareness for fair comparison between density-preserving and sparse representations.
dsp_prompt: Recent studies show that despite advancements in compressing large language models (LLMs), perplexity remains a flawed metric for evaluating sparse representations, leading to significant performance losses during pruning and quantization processes. LLM-KICK introduces a novel evaluation framework that highlights the limitations of current compression techniques across various LLM functionalities, emphasizing the importance of exploring alternative strategies for optimizing LLM efficiency.

titles: Investigating and Simplifying Masking-based Saliency Methods for Model Interpretability
keywords: saliency maps; interpretability; explainable AI; image recognition; image masking; adversarial training
abstracts: Saliency maps that identify the most informative regions of an image for a classifier are valuable for model interpretability. A common approach to creating saliency maps involves generating input masks that mask out portions of an image to maximally deteriorate classification performance, or mask in an image to preserve classification performance. Many variants of this approach have been proposed in the literature, such as counterfactual generation and optimizing over a Gumbel-Softmax distribution. Using a general formulation of masking-based saliency methods, we conduct an extensive evaluation study of a number of recently proposed variants to understand which elements of these methods meaningfully improve performance. Surprisingly, we find that a well-tuned, relatively simple formulation of a masking-based saliency model outperforms many more complex approaches. We find that the most important ingredients for high quality saliency map generation are (1) using both masked-in and masked-out objectives and (2) training the classifier alongside the masking model. Strikingly, we show that a masking model can be trained with as few as 10 examples per class and still generate saliency maps with only a 0.7-point increase in localization error.
one_sentence_summary: In a large evaluation study, we show that a simple formulation of masking-based saliency map generation outperforms many recently proposed improvements, and that comparable results can be obtained by training on as few as 10 examples per class.
standard_prompt: A recent investigation reveals that a simplified, dual-objective masking-based saliency method significantly outperforms more complex alternatives by incorporating both masked-in and masked-out objectives and jointly training the classifier and masking model.
cot_prompt: A novel analysis reveals that a simplified, multi-objective masking-based saliency method significantly outperforms complex alternatives, emphasizing the importance of incorporating both masked-in and masked-out objectives during training.
dsp_prompt: A surprisingly simple variant of a masking-based saliency method significantly outperformed more complex alternatives by combining both masked-in and masked-out objectives during training and utilizing minimal labeled data, highlighting the importance of balanced training objectives and efficient labeling strategies for enhancing image saliency map accuracy while maintaining interpretability.

titles: Neural Representations in Multi-Task Learning guided by Task-Dependent Contexts
keywords: Learning Representations; Neural Geometry; Context-Dependent Decision Making; Attention Mechanisms
abstracts:
The ability to switch between tasks effectively in response to external stimuli is a hallmark of cognitive control. Our brain is able to filter and to integrate external information to accomplish goal-directed behavior. Task switching occurs rapidly and efficiently, allowing us to perform multiple tasks with ease. In a similar way, deep learning models can be tailored to exhibit multi-task capabilities and achieve high performance across domains. Still, understanding how neural networks make predictions is crucial in many real-world applications.

In this study, we delve into neural representations learned by multi-tasking architectures. Concretely, we compare individual and parallel networks with task switching networks. Task-switching networks leverage task-dependent contexts to learn disentangled representations without hurting the overall task accuracy. We show that task-switching networks operate in an intermediate regime between individual and parallel. In addition, we show that shared representations are produced by the emergence neurons encoding multiple tasks. Furthermore, we study the role of contexts across network processing and show its role at aligning the task with the relevant features. Finally, we investigate how the magnitude of contexts affects the performance in task-switching networks.
one_sentence_summary: We investigate neural representations learned by multi-task architectures focusing on task-switching networks that use task-dependent contexts.
standard_prompt: Our study explores neural representations in multi-task learning, revealing that task-switching networks employ context-dependent strategies to balance rapid task switching with accurate domain generalization, thereby enhancing their performance across diverse tasks.
cot_prompt: Our research explores neural representations in multi-task learning using task-switching networks, revealing that they balance task accuracy with disentangled representations and emphasize context alignment for enhanced performance.
dsp_prompt: Our study explores how multi-tasking neural networks employ task-dependent contexts to balance rapid task switching with maintaining accurate task performance, demonstrating that such networks utilize emerging neuron representations for disentangled feature extraction while showing context-driven alignment in decision-making processes.

titles: Explaining by Imitating: Understanding Decisions by Interpretable Policy Learning
keywords: interpretable policy learning; understanding decision-making
abstracts: Understanding human behavior from observed data is critical for transparency and accountability in decision-making. Consider real-world settings such as healthcare, in which modeling a decision-maker’s policy is challenging—with no access to underlying states, no knowledge of environment dynamics, and no allowance for live experimentation. We desire learning a data-driven representation of decision- making behavior that (1) inheres transparency by design, (2) accommodates partial observability, and (3) operates completely offline. To satisfy these key criteria, we propose a novel model-based Bayesian method for interpretable policy learning (“Interpole”) that jointly estimates an agent’s (possibly biased) belief-update process together with their (possibly suboptimal) belief-action mapping. Through experiments on both simulated and real-world data for the problem of Alzheimer’s disease diagnosis, we illustrate the potential of our approach as an investigative device for auditing, quantifying, and understanding human decision-making behavior.
one_sentence_summary: We present a method for learning interpretable representations of behavior to enable auditing, quantifying, and understanding human decision-making processes.
standard_prompt: Interpole, a novel model-based Bayesian framework, learns interpretable policies for decision-making while accommodating partial observability and operating entirely offline, offering a transparent and accurate representation of human decision-making behavior for applications like healthcare diagnostics.
cot_prompt: A new model called "Interpole" learns interpretable policies through Bayesian inference, addressing challenges in understanding decision-making in partially observable environments, exemplified by its application in diagnosing Alzheimer's disease.
dsp_prompt: Interpol's novel model-based Bayesian method learns interpretable policies while accommodating partial observability and operating entirely offline, offering a transparent and accountable framework for studying human decision-making.

titles: TIME-LAPSE: Learning to say “I don't know” through spatio-temporal uncertainty scoring
keywords: out-of-distribution detection; OOD detection; spatio-temporal; latent-space; sequential; outlier; anomaly
abstracts: Safe deployment of trained ML models requires determining when input samples go out-of-distribution (OOD) and refraining from making uncertain predictions on them. Existing approaches inspect test samples in isolation to estimate their corresponding predictive uncertainty. However, in the real-world, deployed models typically see test inputs consecutively and predict labels continuously over time during inference. In this work, we propose TIME-LAPSE, a spatio-temporal framework for uncertainty scoring that examines the sequence of predictions prior to the current sample to determine its predictive uncertainty. Our key insight is that in-distribution samples will be more “similar” to each other compared to OOD samples, not just over the encoding latent-space but also across time. Specifically, (a) our spatial uncertainty score estimates how different OOD latent-space representations are from those of an in-distribution set using metrics such as Mahalanobis distance and cosine similarity and (b) our temporal uncertainty score determines deviations in correlations over time using representations of past inputs in a non-parametric, sliding-window based algorithm. We evaluate TIME-LAPSE on both audio and vision tasks using public datasets and further benchmark our approach on a challenging, real-world, electroencephalograms (EEG) dataset for seizure detection. We achieve state-of-the-art results for OOD detection in the audio and EEG domain and observe considerable gains in semantically corrected vision benchmarks. We show that TIME-LAPSE is more driven by semantic content compared to other methods, i.e., it is more robust to dataset statistics. We also propose a sequential OOD detection evaluation framework to emulate real-life drift settings and show that TIME-LAPSE outperforms spatial methods significantly.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a spatio-temporal framework, TIME-LAPSE that uses latent space embeddings over time to determine when inputs go out-of-distribution and provide uncertainty estimates.
standard_prompt: TIME-LAPSE is a novel spatio-temporal framework that evaluates the uncertainty of in-distribution inputs by considering both spatial and temporal similarities between samples, achieving superior performance in OOD detection across various domains including audio and vision tasks.
cot_prompt: TIME-LAPSE is a novel spatio-temporal framework that evaluates input sequences' predictive uncertainty by considering both spatial and temporal similarities between in- and out-of-distribution data, achieving superior performance in detecting out-of-distribution instances and improving accuracy in various machine learning applications including EEG seizure detection.
dsp_prompt: TIME-LAPSE, an innovative spatio-temporal framework, enhances uncertainty estimation by considering both spatial and temporal similarities between in-distribution and out-of-distribution data, achieving superior performance in detecting out-of-distribution instances across various domains including audio and vision tasks, with particular success in the challenging context of electroencephalogram seizure detection.

titles: CAMA: A New Framework for Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning  Using Constraint Augmentation
keywords: Safe; Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning; Augmentation
abstracts: With the widespread application of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) in real-life settings, the ability to meet safety constraints has become an urgent problem to solve. For example, it is necessary to avoid collisions to reach a common goal in controlling multiple drones. We address this problem by introducing the Constraint Augmented Multi-Agent framework --- CAMA. CAMA can serve as a plug-and-play module to the popular MARL algorithms, including centralized training, decentralized execution and independent learning frameworks. In our approach, we represent the safety constraint as the sum of discounted safety costs bounded by the predefined value, which we call the safety budget. Experiments demonstrate that CAMA can converge quickly to a high degree of constraint satisfaction and surpasses other state-of-the-art safety counterpart algorithms in both cooperative and competitive settings.
one_sentence_summary: CAMA can combine any SOTA non-safe MARL algorithms to ensure they satisfied added constraints without strong assumptions and complex implementations.
standard_prompt: CAMA, an innovative Constraint Augmented Multi-Agent framework, integrates safety constraints within distributed reinforcement learning algorithms through a novel safety budget representation, enabling rapid convergence to optimal safety performance across various scenarios.
cot_prompt: The Constraint Augmented Multi-Agent (CAMA) framework introduces a novel method for incorporating safety constraints into multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), enabling efficient convergence to high levels of safety while significantly outperforming existing solutions across various scenarios.
dsp_prompt: The Constraint Augmented Multi-Agent (CAMA) framework enables rapid convergence with high constraint satisfaction in multi-agent reinforcement learning, addressing safety concerns through a safety budget representation.

titles: Closed-form Sample Probing for Learning Generative Models in Zero-shot Learning
keywords: zero-shot learning; generative zero-shot learning; generative models
abstracts: Generative model based approaches have led to significant advances in zero-shot learning (ZSL) over the past few years. These approaches typically aim to learn a conditional generator that synthesizes training samples of classes conditioned on class definitions. The final zero-shot learning model is then obtained by training a supervised classification model over the real and/or synthesized training samples of seen and unseen classes, combined. Therefore, naturally, the generative model needs to produce not only relevant samples, but also those that are sufficiently rich for classifier training purposes, which is handled by various heuristics in existing works. In this paper, we introduce a principled approach for training generative models {\em directly} for training data generation purposes. Our main observation is that the use of closed-form models opens doors to end-to-end training thanks to the differentiability of the solvers. In our approach, at each generative model update step, we fit a task-specific closed-form ZSL model from generated samples, and measure its loss on novel samples all within the compute graph, a procedure that we refer to as {\em sample probing}. In this manner, the generator receives feedback directly based on the value of its samples for model training purposes. Our experimental results show that the proposed sample probing approach improves the ZSL results even when integrated into state-of-the-art generative models.
one_sentence_summary: We show how to train a conditional generative model in a way that directly maximizes the value of its samples for zero-shot model training purposes.
standard_prompt: In this study, the authors propose a new method called "sample probing" to train generative models directly using closed-form models, which allows for end-to-end training and better performance in zero-shot learning tasks.
cot_prompt: In this paper, the authors propose a new method called "sample probing" to train generative models directly using closed-form solutions, thereby improving zero-shot learning performance through feedback from generated samples.
dsp_prompt: In this study, the authors propose a method called "sample probing" where they train a generative model to directly learn a closed-form discriminative classifier using sampled data, achieving improved performance in zero-shot learning tasks.

titles: MEGAN: Multi Explanation Graph Attention Network
keywords: explainable artificial intelligence; interpretable machine learning; graph neural networks; attention network; graph regression; graph classification
abstracts: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods are expected to improve trust during human-AI interactions, provide tools for model analysis and extend human understanding of complex problems. Attention-based models are an important subclass of XAI methods, partly due to their full differentiability and the potential to improve explanations by means of explanation-supervised training. We propose the novel multi-explanation graph attention network (MEGAN). Our graph regression and classification model features multiple explanation channels, which can be chosen independently of the task specifications. We first validate our model on a synthetic graph regression dataset, where our model produces single-channel explanations with quality similar to GNNExplainer. Furthermore, we demonstrate the advantages of multi-channel explanations on one synthetic and two real-world datasets: The prediction of water solubility of molecular graphs and sentiment classification of movie reviews. We find that our model produces explanations consistent with human intuition, opening the way to learning from our model in less well-understood tasks.
one_sentence_summary: Novel, self-explaining graph attention network features multiple explanation channels independent of task specifications to improve interpretability of graph regression and classification problems
standard_prompt: The novel multi-explanation graph attention network (MEGAN), featuring independent channels for generating diverse explanations, demonstrates superior performance across various domains including synthetic and real-world datasets, achieving consistency with human intuition through its ability to produce coherent and interpretable explanations.
cot_prompt: The novel Multi-Explanation Graph Attention Network (MEGAN) effectively combines multiple explanation channels for better, more interpretable predictions across various domains, showcasing its potential in improving trust and insight through XAI techniques.
dsp_prompt: The novel multi-explanation graph attention network (MEGAN), proposed to address limitations of traditional attention-based models, outperforms existing methods in generating high-quality, interpretable explanations across various domains including graph regression and classification, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving the accuracy and comprehensibility of AI predictions.

titles: Pushing the bounds of dropout
keywords: dropout; language
abstracts: We push on the boundaries of our knowledge about dropout by showing theoretically that dropout training can be understood as performing MAP estimation concurrently for an entire family of conditional models whose objectives are themselves lower bounded by the original dropout objective. This discovery allows us to pick any model from this family after training, which leads to a substantial improvement on regularisation-heavy language modelling. The family includes models that compute a power mean over the sampled dropout masks, and their less stochastic subvariants with tighter and higher lower bounds than the fully stochastic dropout objective. The deterministic subvariant's bound is equal to its objective, and the highest amongst these models. It also exhibits the best model fit in our experiments. Together, these results suggest that the predominant view of deterministic dropout as a good approximation to MC averaging is misleading. Rather, deterministic dropout is the best available approximation to the true objective.
one_sentence_summary: A new view of dropout training as optimizing lower bound for an entire family of models.
standard_prompt: Our work reveals that dropout training can be interpreted as MAP estimation across a family of conditional models, leading to improved regularization and better model fit compared to regular dropout, suggesting that deterministic dropout approximates the true objective more accurately than previously thought.
cot_prompt: We show that dropout training can be interpreted as performing maximum a-posteriori (MAP) estimation across an entire family of conditional models, enabling improved regularization and better model performance through various subvariants of the dropout objective.
dsp_prompt: The authors show that dropout training can be interpreted as performing MAP estimation for a family of conditional models, leading to improved regularization and better model fit compared to traditional approaches.

titles: Efficient Modulation for Vision Networks
keywords: EfficientMod; Efficient Networks
abstracts: In this work, we present efficient modulation, a novel design for efficient vision networks. We revisit the modulation mechanism, which operates input through convolutional context modeling and feature projection layers, and fuses features via element-wise multiplication and an MLP block. We demonstrate that the abstracted modulation mechanism is particularly well suited for efficient networks and further tailor the modulation design by proposing the efficient modulation (EfficientMod) block, which is considered the essential building block for our networks. Bene- fiting from the prominent representational ability of modulation mechanism and the efficiency of efficient modulation design, our network can accomplish better accuracy-efficiency trade-offs and set new state-of-the-art performance for efficient networks. When integrating EfficientMod block with the vanilla self-attention block, we obtain the hybrid architecture and further improve the performance without sacrificing the efficiency. We carry out comprehensive experiments to verify EfficientMod’s performance. With fewer parameters, our EfficientMod-s performs 0.6 top-1 accuracy better than the prior state-of-the-art approach EfficientFormerV2-s2 without any training tricks and is 25% faster on GPU. Additionally, our method presents a notable improvement in downstream tasks, outperforming EfficientFormerV2-s by 3.6 mIoU on the ADE20K benchmark. Code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/ma-xu/EfficientMod.
one_sentence_summary: In this study, we introduce Efficient Modulation (EfficientMod), a novel design for efficient networks that oupforms other methods in terms of both results and latency.
standard_prompt: In this study, the authors introduce the "efficient modulation" technique, enhancing both the accuracy and efficiency of vision networks by optimizing the modulated operation within the CNN framework, achieving superior results over existing methods like EfficientFormerV2-s.
cot_prompt: The authors introduce EfficientMod, a modified version of the modulation technique applied to neural networks, achieving superior accuracy-efficiency trade-offs while being significantly more computationally efficient compared to existing methods.
dsp_prompt: The EfficientMod design introduces an improved modulation mechanism within convolutional neural networks, significantly enhancing their efficiency while maintaining high accuracy, demonstrating superior performance over existing methods on various benchmarks including object detection tasks, achieving notable improvements in both accuracy and speed.

titles: Learning to Observe with Reinforcement Learning
keywords: Reinforcement learning; observation strategies; active data collection
abstracts: We consider a decision making problem where an autonomous agent decides on which actions to take based on the observations it collects from the environment. We are interested in revealing the information structure of the observation space illustrating which type of observations are the most important (such as position versus velocity) and the dependence of this on the state of agent (such as at the bottom versus top of a hill). We approach this problem by associating a cost with collecting observations which increases with the accuracy. We adopt a reinforcement learning (RL) framework where the RL agent learns to adjust the accuracy of the observations alongside learning to perform the original task. We consider both the scenario where the accuracy can be adjusted continuously and also the scenario where the agent has to choose between given preset levels, such as taking a sample perfectly or not taking a sample at all.   In contrast to the existing work that mostly focuses on sample efficiency during training, our focus is on the behaviour during the actual task. Our results illustrate that the RL agent can  learn to use the observation space efficiently and obtain satisfactory performance in the original task while collecting effectively smaller amount of data. By uncovering the relative usefulness of different types of observations and trade-offs within, these results also provide insights for further design of active data acquisition schemes.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a reinforcement learning based active data acqusition framework which reveals the information structure of the observation space demonstrating the type of observations that are the most important during the actual operation of the agent.
standard_prompt: The study explores how a reinforcement learning agent optimally utilizes varying observation accuracies to enhance its performance in tasks, particularly focusing on distinguishing between distinct observation types and balancing their importance in achieving desired outcomes.

titles: DiffusionCLIP: Text-guided Image Manipulation Using Diffusion Models
keywords: Diffusion models; CLIP; Image manipulation; Image to image translation
abstracts: Diffusion models are recent generative models that have shown great success in image generation with the state-of-the-art performance. However, only a few researches have been conducted for image manipulation with diffusion models. Here, we present a novel DiffusionCLIP which performs text-driven image manipulation with diffusion models using Contrastive Language–Image Pre-training (CLIP) loss. Our method has a performance comparable to that of the modern GAN-based image processing methods for in and out-of-domain image processing tasks, with the advantage of almost perfect inversion even without additional encoders or optimization. Furthermore, our method can be easily used for various novel applications, enabling image translation from an unseen domain to another unseen domain or stroke-conditioned image generation in an unseen domain, etc. Finally, we present a novel multiple attribute control with DiffusionCLIP by combining multiple fine-tuned diffusion models.
one_sentence_summary: we present a DiffusionCLIP which performs text-driven image manipulation with diffusion models using CLIP with the advantage of almost perfect inversion.
standard_prompt: DiffusionCLIP, leveraging Diffusion models and CLIP loss, offers competitive performance in text-driven image manipulation, achieving near-perfect image inversion and versatile applications such as domain-specific image translation and stroke-conditioned generation, demonstrating its potential across diverse domains.
cot_prompt: DiffusionCLIP leverages diffusion models and CLIP contrastive loss to achieve high-performance text-driven image manipulation, offering near-perfect inversion capabilities and versatile application potential across different domains.
dsp_prompt: DiffusionCLIP leverages contrastive language-image pre-training to achieve high-performance text-guided image manipulation using diffusion models, demonstrating superior performance over traditional approaches like Generative Adversarial Networks while offering seamless versatility for diverse applications including image translation and stroke-conditioned image generation.

titles: Solving Constrained Variational Inequalities via a First-order Interior Point-based Method
keywords: constrained variational inequality; interior point; admm
abstracts: We develop an interior-point approach to solve constrained variational inequality (cVI) problems. Inspired by the efficacy of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) method in the single-objective context, we generalize ADMM to derive a first-order method for cVIs, that we refer to as ADMM-based interior-point method for constrained VIs (ACVI). We provide convergence guarantees for ACVI in two general classes of problems: (i) when the operator is $\xi$-monotone, and (ii) when it is monotone, some constraints are active and the game is not purely rotational. When the operator is in addition L-Lipschitz for the latter case, we match known lower bounds on rates for the gap function of $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{K})$ and $\mathcal{O}(1/K)$ for the last and average iterate, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first presentation of a first-order interior-point method for the general cVI problem that has a global convergence guarantee. Moreover, unlike previous work in this setting, ACVI provides a means to solve cVIs when the constraints are nontrivial. Empirical analyses demonstrate clear advantages of ACVI over common first-order methods. In particular, (i) cyclical behavior is notably reduced as our methods approach the solution from the analytic center, and (ii) unlike projection-based methods that zigzag when near a constraint, ACVI efficiently handles the constraints.
one_sentence_summary: We derive a first-order method for solving constrained variational inequality problem when given general constraints, by combining interior-point methods and ADMM.
standard_prompt: An interior-point approach based on the alternating direction method of multipliers is developed to solve constrained variational inequalities, achieving global convergence guarantees under specific conditions and outperforming traditional first-order methods through its ability to handle non-trivial constraints effectively.
cot_prompt: We propose the Alternating Direction Multiplier Method with Proximal Linearization (ADMM)-based Interior-Point Algorithm for solving constrained variational inequalities, achieving global convergence guarantees and improved performance compared to existing methods due to its ability to handle non-trivial constraints.
dsp_prompt: We present a novel first-order interior-point algorithm, ACVI, for solving constrained variational inequalities (cVIs), offering convergence guarantees under specific conditions and demonstrating superior performance compared to existing methods in handling non-trivial constraints and reducing cyclical behavior.

titles: Stacked U-Nets: A No-Frills Approach to Natural Image Segmentation
keywords: semantic segmentation; stacked u-nets; classification
abstracts: Many imaging tasks require global information about all pixels in an image. Conventional bottom-up classification networks globalize information by decreasing resolution; features are pooled and down-sampled into a single output. But for semantic segmentation and object detection tasks, a network must provide higher-resolution pixel-level outputs. To globalize information while preserving resolution, many researchers propose the inclusion of sophisticated auxiliary blocks, but these come at the cost of a considerable increase in network size and computational cost. This paper proposes stacked u-nets (SUNets), which iteratively combine features from different resolution scales while maintaining resolution. SUNets leverage the information globalization power of u-nets in a deeper net- work architectures that is capable of handling the complexity of natural images. SUNets perform extremely well on semantic segmentation tasks using a small number of parameters.
one_sentence_summary: Presents new architecture which leverages information globalization power of u-nets in a deeper networks and performs well across tasks without any bells and whistles.
standard_prompt: Stacked u-nets, or SUNets, iteratively combine features from multiple resolutions within a deep neural network architecture, offering efficient and effective semantic segmentation with minimal parameter requirements.
cot_prompt: SUNets, a novel deep learning architecture, combines features from multiple resolutions within a stacked structure, significantly improving segmentation performance with minimal computational overhead.
dsp_prompt: Stacked u-nets, a novel approach, iteratively combines feature scaling with globalization through multiple resolutions to enhance semantic segmentation performance with minimal parameter overhead.

titles: Space-Time Attention with Shifted Non-Local Search
keywords: space-time attention; non-local search; video denoising
abstracts: Efficiently computing attention maps for videos is challenging due to the motion of objects between frames. While a standard non-local search is high-quality for a window surrounding each query point, the window's small size cannot accommodate motion. Methods for long-range motion use an auxiliary network to predict the most similar key coordinates as offsets from each query location. However, accurately predicting this flow field of offsets remains challenging, even for large-scale networks. Small spatial inaccuracies significantly impact the attention module's quality. This paper proposes a search strategy that combines the quality of a non-local search with the range of predicted offsets. The method, named Shifted Non-Local Search, executes a small grid search surrounding the predicted offsets to correct small spatial errors. Our method's in-place computation consumes 10 times less memory and is over 3 times faster than previous work. Experimentally, correcting the small spatial errors improves the video frame alignment quality by over 3 dB PSNR. Our search upgrades existing space-time attention modules, which improves video denoising results by 0.30 dB PSNR for a 7.5\% increase in overall runtime. We integrate our space-time attention module into a UNet-like architecture to achieve state-of-the-art results on video denoising.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a Shifted Non-Local Search module to improve the quality of space-time attention by correcting the small spatial errors of offsets predicted from an auxiliary network.
standard_prompt: A novel shift-based non-local search strategy for improving accuracy and efficiency in space-time attention computations within videos, enhancing performance up to 3 dB PSNR and reducing runtime by 7.5%, achieving state-of-the-art results through integration into a UNet-like architecture.
cot_prompt: A novel Shifted Non-Local Search algorithm enhances video attention by combining the efficiency of a standard non-local search with improved accuracy in predicting offset flows, resulting in significant improvements in video frame alignment and denoising performance while reducing computational costs and increasing speed.
dsp_prompt: A novel "Shifted Non-Local Search" technique enhances space-time attention in videos by combining the accuracy of local searches with the predictive power of auxiliary networks, leading to improved frame alignment and enhanced video denoising performance.

titles: Grounded Object-Centric Learning
keywords: object-centric representation learning; the binding problem; the grounding problem; slot attention
abstracts: The extraction of object-centric representations for downstream tasks is an emerging area of research. Learning grounded representations of objects that are guaranteed to be stable and invariant promises robust performance across different tasks and environments. Slot Attention (SA) learns object-centric representations by assigning objects to *slots*, but presupposes a *single* distribution from which all slots are randomly initialised. This results in an inability to learn *specialized* slots which bind to specific object types and remain invariant to identity-preserving changes in object appearance. To address this, we present *Conditional Slot Attention* (CoSA) using a novel concept of *Grounded Slot Dictionary* (GSD) inspired by vector quantization. Our proposed GSD comprises (i) canonical object-level property vectors and (ii) parametric Gaussian distributions, which define a prior over the slots. We demonstrate the benefits of our method in multiple downstream tasks such as scene generation, composition, and task adaptation, whilst remaining competitive with SA in object discovery.
one_sentence_summary: We propose conditional slot attention model to learn specialized slots which bind to specific object types and remain invariant to identity-preserving changes in object appearance.
standard_prompt: The authors introduce Conditional Slot Attention (CoSA), a variant of Slot Attention that utilizes a Grounded Slot Dictionary (GSD) consisting of canonical object-level property vectors and parametric Gaussian distributions, enabling the learning of specialized object-centric representations that maintain stability and invariance across different tasks and environments.
cot_prompt: Conditional Slot Attention (CoSA), utilizing a Grounded Slot Dictionary (GSD) consisting of canonical property vectors and parametric Gaussian distributions, addresses limitations of Single-Source Initialization in Slot Attention, enhancing specialization and stability across diverse object-related tasks and environments.
dsp_prompt: Our proposed Conditional Slot Attention (CoSA) leverages a Grounded Slot Dictionary (GSD), combining canonical property vectors and parametric Gaussian distributions, to address the "binding problem" in object-centric representation learning, demonstrating superior performance in various downstream tasks while maintaining competitiveness with traditional Slot Attention methods like SA.

titles: Cyclophobic Reinforcement Learning
keywords: Reinforcement learning; intrinsic rewards; exploration; transfer learning; objects
abstracts: In environments with sparse rewards finding a good inductive bias for exploration is crucial to the agent’s success. However, there are two competing goals: novelty search and systematic exploration. While existing approaches such as curiousity- driven exploration find novelty, they sometimes do not systematically explore the whole state space, akin to depth-first-search vs breadth-first-search. In this paper, we propose a new intrinsic reward that is cyclophobic, i.e. it does not reward novelty, but punishes redundancy by avoiding cycles. Augmenting the cyclophobic intrinsic reward with a sequence of hierarchical representations based on the agent’s cropped observations we are able to achieve excellent results in the MiniGrid and MiniHack environments. Both are particularly hard, as they require complex interactions with different objects in order to be solved. Detailed comparisons with previous approaches and thorough ablation studies show that our newly proposed cyclophobic reinforcement learning is vastly more efficient than other state of the art methods.
one_sentence_summary: Cyclophobic Reinforcement Learning systematically and efficiently explores the state space by penalizing cycles, achieving excellent results in sparse reward environements.
standard_prompt: In environments like MiniGrid and MiniHack where agents must navigate complex scenarios involving diverse objects, a novel cyclophobic intrinsic reward mechanism significantly enhances efficiency through its avoidance of redundant cycles, leading to superior performance compared to current methods across various challenges.
cot_prompt: A novel cyclophobic intrinsic reward mechanism significantly enhances exploration efficiency in challenging environments like MiniGrid and MiniHack, achieving superior performance through augmented hierarchical observation representations.
