We instead propose Locality-sENSitive (LENS) improvements of the above metrics, namely, LENS-top-$k$, LENS-Spearman and LENS-Kendall, that incorporate the locality of attributions along with their rank order. Our locality-sensitive metrics provide tighter bounds on attributional robustness and do not disproportionately penalize attribution methods for reasonable local changes. We show that the robust attribution methods proposed in recent works also reflect this premise of locality, thus highlighting the need for a locality-sensitive metric for progress in the field. Our empirical results on well-known benchmark datasets using well-known models and attribution methods support our observations and conclusions in this work.
one_sentence_summary: The existing metrics for robustness of attributions to small impercetible perturbations don't capture local sensitivity. We propose new locality-sensitive metrics and show their usefulness.
standard_prompt: Recent studies highlight the fragility of existing attribution metrics, which often fail to accurately capture the impact of small perturbations, leading to the development of Locality-sensitive Metrics (LENS) for better understanding and robustness in machine learning models.
cot_prompt: Recent works highlight the fragility of existing attribution metrics like top-$k$ intersection, Spearman's rank-order correlation, and Kendall's rank-order in measuring attributional robustness due to their reliance on global rather than localized changes in feature attributions. The authors propose Local-SENSitive (LENS) improvements to address this issue by incorporating the locality of attributions, showing that traditional robust attribution methods often align with this principle, underscoring the necessity for a locality-sensitive metric in evaluating robustness.
dsp_prompt: Recent efforts in improving attribution methods through locality-sensitive metrics like LENS have highlighted the importance of considering the local nature of attributions when measuring robustness, suggesting that traditional metrics may overestimate the impact of minor perturbations.

titles: Behaviour Suite for Reinforcement Learning
keywords: reinforcement learning; benchmark; core issues; scalability; reproducibility
abstracts: This paper introduces the Behaviour Suite for Reinforcement Learning, or bsuite for short. bsuite is a collection of carefully-designed experiments that investigate core capabilities of reinforcement learning (RL) agents with two objectives. First, to collect clear, informative and scalable problems that capture key issues in the design of general and efficient learning algorithms. Second, to study agent behaviour through their performance on these shared benchmarks. To complement this effort, we open source this http URL, which automates evaluation and analysis of any agent on bsuite. This library facilitates reproducible and accessible research on the core issues in RL, and ultimately the design of superior learning algorithms. Our code is Python, and easy to use within existing projects. We include examples with OpenAI Baselines, Dopamine as well as new reference implementations. Going forward, we hope to incorporate more excellent experiments from the research community, and commit to a periodic review of bsuite from a committee of prominent researchers.
one_sentence_summary: Bsuite is a collection of carefully-designed experiments that investigate the core capabilities of RL agents.
standard_prompt: The Behavior Suite for Reinforcement Learning (bsuite) is a collection of benchmark experiments designed to address fundamental challenges in reinforcement learning, providing a standardized framework for evaluating and comparing different AI agents.
cot_prompt: The Behavior Suite for Reinforcement Learning, or bsuite, is a collection of experiments designed to address key challenges in reinforcement learning by providing standardized benchmarking tools, facilitating collaborative research, and enabling developers to easily integrate bsuite into their projects via Python-based libraries and example implementations.
dsp_prompt: The Behavior Suite for Reinforcement Learning (bsuite) is a collection of carefully designed experiments aimed at collecting clear, informative, and scalable benchmarks for studying core capabilities and behavior of reinforcement learning agents, facilitating reproducible and accessible research by automating evaluations and analyses across various agents using Python libraries like OpenAI Baselines and Dopamine.

titles: Learning Object-Centric Dynamic Modes from Video and Emerging Properties
keywords: Koopman theory; dynamics; video representation learning; dynamic mode decomposition; video manipulation; object-centric decomposition
abstracts: One of the long-term objectives of Artificial Intelligence  is to endow machines with the capacity of structuring and interpreting the world as we do. Towards this goal, recent methods have successfully  decomposed and disentangled video sequences into their composing objects, attributes and dynamics, in a self-supervised fashion. However, there have been scarce efforts to propose useful decompositions of the dynamics in a scene. We propose a method to decompose a video into moving objects, their attributes and the dynamic modes of their trajectories. We model the objects' dynamics with linear system identification tools, by means of a Koopman mapping and the Koopman operator $\mathcal{K}$. This allows user access and interpretation of the dynamics in the scene. We test our framework in a variety of datasets, while illustrating the novel features that emerge from our dynamic modes decomposition: temporal super-resolution, backwards forecasting, model reduction and video dynamics interpretation and manipulation at test-time. We successfully forecast challenging object trajectories from pixels, achieving competitive performance while drawing useful insights.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a model for dynamics interpretability and manipulation by means of object-centric dynamic mode decomposition, directly from pixels.
standard_prompt: We introduce a dynamic modes decomposition framework for videos using linear system identification, allowing users to analyze and manipulate the dynamics of moving objects within scenes through Koopman operators, showcasing improved temporal resolution, backward forecasting capabilities, reduced models, and enhanced understanding of video motion.
cot_prompt: Our method models video scenes using linear systems identified through Koopman operators, enabling dynamic mode decomposition for improved temporal super-resolution, backward forecasting, reduced complexity, and intuitive analysis of complex object movements.
dsp_prompt: Our method uses Koopman theory to identify and interpret complex video dynamics through object-centric decomposition, enabling tasks like super-resolution, backward forecasting, and manipulating object trajectories from raw pixel data, showcasing its potential for enhancing AI's understanding and manipulation of visual scenes.

titles: Explaining Image Classifiers by Counterfactual Generation
keywords: Explainability; Interpretability; Generative Models; Saliency Map; Machine Learning; Deep Learning
abstracts: When an image classifier makes a prediction, which parts of the image are relevant and why? We can rephrase this question to ask: which parts of the image, if they were not seen by the classifier, would most change its decision? Producing an answer requires marginalizing over images that could have been seen but weren't. We can sample plausible image in-fills by conditioning a generative model on the rest of the image. We then optimize to find the image regions that most change the classifier's decision after in-fill. Our approach contrasts with ad-hoc in-filling approaches, such as blurring or injecting noise, which generate inputs far from the data distribution, and ignore informative relationships between different parts of the image. Our method produces more compact and relevant saliency maps, with fewer artifacts compared to previous methods.
one_sentence_summary: We compute saliency by using a strong generative model to efficiently marginalize over plausible alternative inputs, revealing concentrated pixel areas that preserve label information.
standard_prompt: Our method generates more accurate and contextually relevant explanations for image classifiers through counterfactual reasoning, optimizing image regions that significantly alter predictions based on partial in-fill samples.
cot_prompt: Our approach generates more accurate and less noisy saliency maps by infilling images using a generative model conditioned on the rest of the image, optimizing for changes in classification decisions.
dsp_prompt: Our novel approach uses generative models to condition on missing parts of images, optimizing for changes in classifiers' decisions when filled in, producing more accurate and interpretable saliency maps compared to existing methods.

titles: Proximal Curriculum with Task Correlations for Deep Reinforcement Learning
keywords: curriculum design; reinforcement learning
abstracts: Curriculum design for reinforcement learning (RL) can speed up an agent's learning process and help it learn to perform well on complex tasks. However, existing techniques typically require domain-specific hyperparameter tuning, involve expensive optimization procedures for task selection, or are suitable only for specific learning objectives. In this work, we consider curriculum design in contextual multi-task settings where the agent's final performance is measured w.r.t. a target distribution over complex tasks. We base our curriculum design on the Zone of Proximal Development concept, which has proven to be effective in accelerating the learning process of RL agents for uniform distribution over all tasks. We propose a novel curriculum, ProxCoRL, that effectively balances the need for selecting tasks that are not too difficult for the agent while progressing the agent's learning toward the target distribution via leveraging task correlations. We theoretically justify the task selection strategy of ProxCoRL by analyzing a simple learning setting with REINFORCE learner model. Our experimental results across various domains with challenging target task distributions affirm the effectiveness of our curriculum strategy over state-of-the-art baselines in accelerating the training process of deep RL agents.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a curriculum strategy for reinforcement learning agents that picks a training task based on the agent's performance on the task and its correlation with tasks in the target distribution.
standard_prompt: ProxCoRL, based on the Zone of Proximal Development, uses a curriculum designed around task correlations to accelerate the learning process of deep reinforcement learning agents towards a target distribution over diverse tasks.
cot_prompt: ProxCoRL, a curriculum designed around task correlations, accelerates deep reinforcement learning through efficient task selection strategies, particularly beneficial for tackling complex, challenging environments.
dsp_prompt: ProxCoRL, a novel curriculum designed based on the Zone of Proximal Development concept, efficiently selects diverse yet challenging tasks for deep reinforcement learning agents to accelerate their learning towards a target distribution through leveraging task correlations, demonstrating superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods across various domains.

titles: Can Neural Networks Understand Logical Entailment?
keywords: structure; neural networks; logic; dataset
abstracts: We introduce a new dataset of logical entailments for the purpose of measuring models' ability to capture and exploit the structure of logical expressions against an entailment prediction task. We use this task to compare a series of architectures which are ubiquitous in the sequence-processing literature, in addition to a new model class---PossibleWorldNets---which computes entailment as a ``convolution over possible worlds''. Results show that convolutional networks present the wrong inductive bias for this class of problems relative to LSTM RNNs, tree-structured neural networks outperform LSTM RNNs due to their enhanced ability to exploit the syntax of logic, and PossibleWorldNets outperform all benchmarks.
one_sentence_summary: We introduce a new dataset of logical entailments for the purpose of measuring models' ability to capture and exploit the structure of logical expressions against an entailment prediction task.
standard_prompt: A study introduces a novel dataset to measure logical entailment understanding by comparing various deep learning architectures, finding that convolutional networks fail at capturing logical structures while LSTM-based approaches excel through syntax exploitation, with PossibleWorldNets surpassing all methods.
cot_prompt: Neural network models struggle with logical entailment tasks compared to LSTM RNNs and tree-structured neural networks, but PossibleWorldNets excel at exploiting logical syntax.
dsp_prompt: A comparison between different neural network architectures reveals that PossibleWorldNets excel at capturing and exploiting the structure of logical expressions, demonstrating superior performance compared to traditional methods like LSTMs and tree-structured neural networks when applied to logical entailment tasks.

titles: FedBug: A Bottom-Up Gradual Unfreezing Framework for Federated Learning With Client Drift
keywords: federated learning; decentralized learning
abstracts: Federated Learning (FL) offers a collaborative training framework, allowing multiple clients to contribute to a shared model without compromising data privacy. Due to the heterogeneous nature of local datasets, updated client models may overfit and diverge from one another, commonly known as the problem of client drift. In this paper, we propose FedBug (Federated Learning with Bottom-Up Gradual Unfreezing), a novel FL framework designed to effectively mitigate client drift. FedBug adaptively leverages the client model parameters, distributed by the server at each global round, as the reference points for cross-client alignment. Specifically, on the client side, FedBug begins by freezing the entire model, then gradually unfreezes the layers, from the input layer to the output layer. This bottom-up approach allows models to train the newly thawed layers to project data into a latent space, wherein the separating hyperplanes remain consistent across all clients. We theoretically analyze FedBug in a novel over-parameterization FL setup, revealing its superior convergence rate compared to FedAvg. Through comprehensive experiments, spanning various datasets, training conditions, and network architectures, we validate the efficacy of FedBug. Our contributions encompass a novel FL framework, theoretical analysis, and empirical validation, demonstrating the potential and wide applicability of FedBug.
one_sentence_summary: We propose FedBug, a novel federated learning framework that leverages model parameters as anchors to effectively address client drift in federated learning.
standard_prompt: FedBug, a novel federated learning framework that progressively unfreezes client models through a bottom-up approach, adapts the entire model during initial stages, freezes layers sequentially, and uses a latent space to maintain consistent separating hyperplanes across diverse clients, enhancing convergence rates and effectiveness in managing client drift in federated learning environments.
cot_prompt: FedBug, a novel federated learning framework, employs a bottom-up gradual unfreezing strategy to align client models during training, addressing client drift through adaptive parameter updates and effective model adaptation, showcasing superior performance over traditional methods like FedAvg.
dsp_prompt: FedBug, a novel federated learning framework, adaptsively freezes and gradually unfreezes client model parameters in a bottom-up manner, enabling effective mitigation of client drift through adaptive cross-client alignment, achieving superior convergence rates in a novel over-parameterization setting.

titles: FedFA:  Federated Feature Augmentation
keywords: federated learning; feature augmentation
abstracts: Federated learning is a distributed paradigm that allows multiple parties to collaboratively train deep models without exchanging the raw data. However, the data distribution among clients is naturally non-i.i.d., which leads to severe degradation of the learnt model. The primary goal of this paper is to develop a robust federated learning algorithm to address feature shift in clients’ samples, which can be caused by various factors, e.g., acquisition differences in medical imaging. To reach this goal, we propose FedFA to tackle federated learning from a dis- tinct perspective of federated feature augmentation. FedFA is based on a major insight that each client’s data distribution can be characterized by statistics (i.e., mean and standard deviation) of latent features; and it is likely to manipulate these local statistics globally, i.e., based on information in the entire federation, to let clients have a better sense of the underlying distribution and therefore alleviate local data bias. Based on this insight, we propose to augment each local feature statistic probabilistically based on a normal distribution, whose mean is the original statistic and variance quantifies the augmentation scope. Key to our approach is the determination of a meaningful Gaussian variance, which is accomplished by taking into account not only biased data of each individual client, but also underlying feature statistics characterized by all participating clients. We offer both theoretical and empirical justifications to verify the effectiveness of FedFA. Our code is available at https://github.com/tfzhou/FedFA.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a simple, flexible, effective, and robust method, named as FedFA, to solve federated learning from a novel perspective of federated feature augmentation.
standard_prompt: FedFA, a novel federated learning method, addresses feature shift through statistical augmentation, leveraging global statistics across clients to mitigate local biases and improve model robustness in diverse datasets.
cot_prompt: FedFA proposes a novel method for addressing feature shift in federated learning by augmenting local feature statistics using a Gaussian distribution, leveraging global statistics across the federated dataset to mitigate local biases and improve model generalization.
dsp_prompt: FedFA, a novel method for addressing feature shift through probabilistic feature statistic augmentation, leverages global statistical knowledge derived from the entire federated dataset to enhance model robustness in federated learning scenarios with non-i.i.d. data distributions.

titles: Meta-Learning Nonlinear Dynamical Systems with Deep Kernels
keywords: latent force models; gaussian processes; meta-learning; dynamic model; differential equations
abstracts: Scientific processes are often modelled by sets of differential equations. As datasets grow, individually fitting these models and quantifying their uncertainties becomes a computationally challenging task. In this paper, we focus on improving the scalability of a particular class of stochastic dynamical model, called latent force models. These offer a balance between data-driven and mechanistic inference in dynamical systems, achieved by deriving a kernel function over a low-dimensional latent force. However, exact computation of posterior kernel terms is rarely tractable, requiring approximations for complex scenarios such as nonlinear dynamics. We overcome this issue by posing the problem as meta-learning the class of latent force models corresponding to a set of differential equations. By employing a deep kernel along with a sensible function embedding, we demonstrate the ability to extrapolate from simulations to real experimental datasets. Finally, we show how our model scales compared with other approximations.
one_sentence_summary: We improve the scalability of inferring latent forces under nonlinear dynamics by learning multi-task deep kernels.
standard_prompt: The authors propose a method using deep kernels to improve the scalability of latent force models for non-linear dynamical systems, demonstrating its effectiveness through both simulation and real-world dataset applications.
cot_prompt: Our study proposes a novel meta-learning approach using deep kernels to approximate latent force models, enabling scalable inference across diverse dynamical systems, including nonlinear ones, demonstrating superior performance in both simulation-to-experiment extrapolation and computational efficiency.
dsp_prompt: In this work, we leverage deep kernels to develop a scalable latent force model for non-linear dynamical systems through meta-learning, demonstrating superior performance in both simulation and real-world applications compared to traditional methods.

titles: DIET-SNN: A Low-Latency Spiking Neural Network with Direct Input Encoding & Leakage and Threshold Optimization
keywords: Spiking neural networks; threshold optimization; leak optimization; input encoding; deep convolutional networks
abstracts: Bio-inspired spiking neural networks (SNNs), operating with asynchronous binary signals (or spikes) distributed over time, can potentially lead to greater computational efficiency on event-driven hardware. The state-of-the-art SNNs suffer from high inference latency, resulting from inefficient input encoding, and sub-optimal settings of the neuron parameters (firing threshold, and membrane leak). We propose DIET-SNN, a low latency deep spiking network that is trained with gradient descent to optimize the membrane leak and the firing threshold along with other network parameters (weights). The membrane leak and threshold for each layer of the SNN are optimized with end-to-end backpropagation to achieve competitive accuracy at reduced latency. The analog pixel values of an image are directly applied to the input layer of DIET-SNN without the need to convert to spike-train. The first convolutional layer is trained to convert inputs into spikes where leaky-integrate-and-fire (LIF) neurons integrate the weighted inputs and generate an output spike when the membrane potential crosses the trained firing threshold. The trained membrane leak controls the flow of input information and attenuates irrelevant inputs to increase the activation sparsity in the convolutional and linear layers of the network. The reduced latency combined with high activation sparsity provides large improvements in computational efficiency. We evaluate DIET-SNN on image classification tasks from CIFAR and ImageNet datasets on VGG and ResNet architectures. We achieve top-1 accuracy of 69% with 5 timesteps (inference latency) on the ImageNet dataset with 12x less compute energy than an equivalent standard ANN. Additionally, DIET-SNN performs 20-500x faster inference compared to other state-of-the-art SNN models.
one_sentence_summary: Gradient based training of threshold and leak in deep spiking networks to achieve high activation sparsity and low inference latency
standard_prompt: DIET-SNN, an optimized bio-inspired spiking neural network, achieves high accuracy and reduced latency by optimizing membrane leak and threshold parameters during training, directly applying raw pixel values without conversion, and leveraging LIF neurons for efficient input processing, demonstrating significant performance gains in image classification tasks.
cot_prompt: DIET-SNN, a low-latency bio-inspired deep spiking neural network, achieves significant performance improvements through direct input encoding, optimized neuron parameters, and efficient spike-based processing, outperforming traditional ANNs in terms of both speed and accuracy while reducing computational requirements significantly.
dsp_prompt: DIET-SNN, a novel low-latency spiking neural network utilizing direct input encoding, threshold optimization, and efficient parameter tuning through gradient descent, achieves high accuracy while significantly reducing inference latency by optimizing membrane leaks and thresholds across layers, enabling substantial computational efficiency gains on event-driven hardware, particularly excelling in image classification tasks.

titles: Ask Question with Double Hints:  Visual Question Generation with Answer-awareness and Region-reference
keywords: Semi-supervised Learning; graph neural network; vision and language; question generation
abstracts: The task of visual question generation~(VQG) aims to generate human-like questions from an image and potentially other side information (e.g. answer type or the answer itself). Despite promising results have been achieved, previous works on VQG either i) suffer from one image to many questions mapping problem rendering the failure of generating referential and meaningful questions from an image, or ii) ignore rich correlations among the visual objects in an image and potential interactions between the side information and image. To address these limitations, we first propose a novel learning paradigm to generate visual questions with answer-awareness and region-reference. In particular, we aim to ask the right visual questions with \emph{Double Hints - textual answers and visual regions of interests}, effectively mitigating the existing one-to-many mapping issue. To this end, we develop a simple methodology to self-learn the visual hints without introducing any additional human annotations. Furthermore, to capture these sophisticated relationships, we propose a new double-hints guided Graph-to-Sequence learning framework that first models them as a dynamic graph and learns the implicit topology end-to-end, and then utilize a graph-to-sequence model to generate the questions with double hints. Our experiments on VQA2.0 and COCO-QA datasets demonstrate that our proposed model on this new setting can significantly outperform existing state-of-the-art baselines by a large margin.
one_sentence_summary: For visual question generation task, we propose a new learning paradigm and a novel a double-hints guided graph-to-sequence learning framework to address the one-to-many mapping and object modeling with side information problems.
standard_prompt: Our study introduces a novel method for generating visual questions using answer-awareness and region-reference, addressing issues such as the "one-to-many" mapping problem and ignoring visual object correlations, through a dual hint-driven approach involving a graph-to-sequence model that incorporates visual clues, leading to significant improvements over current methods.
cot_prompt: Our study introduces a novel method for visual question generation using answer-awareness and region-reference, achieving significant improvements over existing approaches through a dynamic graph-to-sequence learning framework.
dsp_prompt: Our novel approach addresses the challenge of visual question generation by incorporating answer-awareness and region-reference through a dual-hint-guided graph-to-sequence learning framework, demonstrating superior performance on both VQA2.0 and COCO-QA datasets compared to current state-of-the-art methods.

titles: Benchmarking Machine Learning Robustness in Covid-19 Spike Sequence Classification
keywords: COVID-19; Sequence Classification; Spike Sequences; k-mers; Deep Learning
abstracts:
The rapid spread of the COVID-19 pandemic has resulted in an unprecedented amount of sequence data of the SARS-CoV-2 viral genome --- millions of sequences and counting.  This amount of data, while being orders of magnitude beyond the capacity of traditional approaches to understanding the diversity, dynamics and evolution of viruses, is nonetheless a rich resource for machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches as alternatives for extracting such important information from these data.  It is of hence utmost importance to design a framework for testing and benchmarking the robustness of these ML and DL approaches.

This paper the first (to our knowledge) to explore such a framework. In this paper, we introduce several ways to perturb SARS-CoV-2 spike protein sequences in ways that mimic the error profiles of common sequencing platforms such as Illumina and PacBio.  We show from experiments on a wide array of ML approaches from naive Bayes to logistic regression, that DL approaches are more robust (and accurate) to such adverarial attacks to the input sequences, while $k$-mer based feature vector representations are more robust than the baseline one-hot embedding.  Our benchmarking framework may developers of futher ML and DL techniques to properly assess their approaches towards understanding the behaviour of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, or towards avoiding possible future pandemics.
one_sentence_summary: In this paper, we test the robustness of deep learning models by creating adversarial spike sequences corresponding to different variants of coronavirus. We establish rigorous benchmarks for spike sequence classification.
standard_prompt: The paper introduces a benchmarking framework for evaluating the robustness of machine learning approaches against adversarial attacks on SARS-CoV-2 spike protein sequences, showing that deep learning methods are generally more resilient compared to other representation types under different sequencing errors.
cot_prompt: The authors present a novel benchmarking framework to evaluate the robustness of machine learning models against adversarial attacks on SARS-CoV-2 spike protein sequences, showing that deep learning methods are generally more resilient compared to other feature representation techniques.
dsp_prompt: The paper introduces a novel framework for evaluating the robustness of machine learning and deep learning approaches to adversarial attacks on SARS-CoV-2 spike protein sequences, showing that deep learning models perform better under perturbed inputs compared to other features like k-mers.

titles: How Two-Layer Networks Learn, One (Giant) Step at a Time
keywords: Feature learning; Gradient descent; SGD; Learning Theory; Two-layers neural network; Random Features
abstracts: We investigate theoretically how the features of a two-layer neural network adapt to the structure of the target function through a few large batch gradient descent steps, leading to improvement in the approximation capacity, but only along the learned directions. We compare the influence of batch size and that of multiple (but finitely many) steps. For a single gradient step, a batch of size $n = \mathcal{O}(d)$ is both necessary and sufficient to align with the target function, although only a single direction can be learned. In contrast, $n = \mathcal{O}(d^2)$ is essential for neurons to specialize to multiple relevant directions of the target with a single gradient step. Even in this case, we show there might exist ``hard'' directions requiring $n = \mathcal{O}(d^\ell)$ samples to be learned, where $\ell$ is known as the leap index of the target. The picture drastically improves over multiple gradient steps: we show that a batch-size of $n = \mathcal{O}(d)$ is indeed enough to learn multiple target directions satisfying a staircase property, where more and more direction can be learned over time. Finally, we discuss how these direction allows to drastically improve generalization over the initialization, illustrating a separation of scale between the random feature/lazy regime, and the feature learning regime. Our technical analysis leverages a combination of techniques related to concentration, projection-based conditioning, and Gaussian equivalence which we believe are of independent interest. By pinning down the conditions necessary for specialization and learning, our results highlight the interaction between batch size and number of iterations, and lead to a hierarchical depiction where learning performance exhibits a stairway to accuracy over time and batch size, shedding new light on how neural networks adapt to features of the data.
one_sentence_summary: Few giants steps of gradient descent on shallow networks are sometimes sufficient to learn beyond the kernel regime, and we are telling when it happens
standard_prompt: In a two-layer neural network, adapting to the structure of the target function through large batches of updates leads to improved approximation capacity by learning specific directions, with different batch sizes affecting the number of directions learned and the rate of specialization, ultimately facilitating better generalization across scales.
cot_prompt: Through theoretical investigation, it is shown that for a two-layer neural network, while a batch size of \( n = \mathcal{O}(d) \) is both necessary and sufficient for alignment with the target function during a single gradient step, larger batches are required for learning multiple relevant directions, with the leap index (\( \ell \)) determining the number of directions that can be learned within a given batch size. This highlights the importance of batch size in achieving high-dimensional representation capabilities.
dsp_prompt: In a two-layer neural network, specialized directions are learned via a few gradient steps, influenced by batch size and the number of steps, highlighting the trade-off between batch size and learning efficiency and revealing a hierarchical learning path towards improved generalization.

titles: Implicit Neural Spatial Representations for Time-dependent PDEs
keywords: PDE; implicit neural representation; neural field; numerical methods
abstracts:
Numerically solving partial differential equations (PDEs) often entails spatial and temporal discretizations. Traditional methods (e.g., finite
difference, finite element, smoothed-particle hydrodynamics) frequently adopt explicit spatial discretizations, such as grids, meshes, and point clouds, where each degree-of-freedom corresponds to a location in space. While these explicit spatial correspondences are intuitive to model and understand, these representations are not necessarily optimal for accuracy, memory-usage, or adaptivity. In this work, we explore implicit neural representation as an alternative spatial discretization, where spatial information is implicitly stored in the neural network weights. With implicit neural spatial representation, PDE-constrained time-stepping translates into updating neural network weights, which naturally integrates with commonly adopted optimization time integrators. We validate our approach on a variety of classic PDEs with examples involving large elastic deformations, turbulent fluids, and multiscale phenomena. While slower to compute than traditional representations, our approach exhibits higher accuracy, lower memory consumption, and dynamically adaptive allocation of degrees of freedom without complex remeshing.
one_sentence_summary: We replace traditional PDE solvers' spatial representations (e.g., grid, mesh, and point cloud) with a neural spatial representation.
standard_prompt: Implicit neural spatial representations offer an alternative to traditional explicit spatial discretizations by storing spatial information within neural network weights, enabling efficient and accurate solution of PDEs through dynamic updates that integrate with common optimization time-integrators.
cot_prompt: Implicit neural spatial representations offer an alternative to traditional grid-based discretizations, enabling faster, more accurate, and adaptable numerical solutions to PDEs through implicit weight updates within neural networks.
dsp_prompt: Implicit neural spatial representations offer an alternative to traditional explicit discretizations by storing spatial information within neural network weights, allowing for improved accuracy, reduced memory usage, and dynamic adaptability in solving time-dependent partial differential equations through integrated optimization and neural update processes.

titles: Predicting Auction Price of Vehicle License Plate with Deep Recurrent Neural Network
keywords: price predictions; expert system; recurrent neural networks; deep learning; natural language processing
abstracts:
In Chinese societies, superstition is of paramount importance, and vehicle license plates with desirable numbers can fetch very high prices in auctions. Unlike other valuable items, license plates are not allocated an estimated price before auction. 

I propose that the task of predicting plate prices can be viewed as a natural language processing (NLP) task, as the value depends on the meaning of each individual character on the plate and its semantics. I construct a deep recurrent neural network (RNN) to predict the prices of vehicle license plates in Hong Kong, based on the characters on a plate. I demonstrate the importance of having a deep network and of retraining. Evaluated on 13 years of historical auction prices, the deep RNN's predictions can explain over 80 percent of price variations, outperforming previous models by a significant margin.  I also demonstrate how the model can be extended to become a search engine for plates and to provide estimates of the expected price distribution.
one_sentence_summary: Predicting auction price of vehicle license plates in Hong Kong with deep recurrent neural network, based on the characters on the plates.
standard_prompt: A deep recurrent neural network predicts vehicle license plate prices using character semantics, achieving higher accuracy than traditional methods over 80% of variation, demonstrating potential for both prediction and personalized pricing services.
cot_prompt: A deep recurrent neural network predicts vehicle license plate prices through NLP, achieving higher accuracy than traditional methods and demonstrating potential applications in searching and pricing estimation.
dsp_prompt: A deep recurrent neural network predicts vehicle license plate prices in Hong Kong using NLP techniques, achieving 80% accuracy compared to traditional methods.

titles: Deep Encoder, Shallow Decoder: Reevaluating Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
keywords: Machine Translation; Sequence Modeling; Natural Language Processing
abstracts: Much recent effort has been invested in non-autoregressive neural machine translation, which appears to be an efficient alternative to state-of-the-art autoregressive machine translation on modern GPUs.  In contrast to the latter, where generation is sequential, the former allows generation to be parallelized across target token positions. Some of the latest non-autoregressive models have achieved impressive translation quality-speed tradeoffs compared to autoregressive baselines. In this work, we reexamine this tradeoff and argue that autoregressive baselines can be substantially sped up without loss in accuracy. Specifically, we study autoregressive models with encoders and decoders of varied depths. Our extensive experiments show that given a sufficiently deep encoder, a single-layer autoregressive decoder can substantially outperform strong non-autoregressive models with comparable inference speed. We show that the speed disadvantage for autoregressive baselines compared to non-autoregressive methods has been overestimated in three aspects: suboptimal layer allocation, insufficient speed measurement, and lack of knowledge distillation. Our results establish a new protocol for future research toward fast, accurate machine translation. Our code is available at https://github.com/jungokasai/deep-shallow.
one_sentence_summary: We show that the speed disadvantage for autoregressive baselines to evaluate non-autoregressive machine translation is overestimated in three aspects: suboptimal layer allocation, insufficient speed measurement, and lack of knowledge distillation.
standard_prompt: Recent advancements in non-autoregressive machine translation highlight its efficiency but also reveal potential for significantly speeding up autoregressive models by leveraging a deeper encoder-decoder architecture, demonstrating substantial performance improvements while maintaining high accuracy and enabling faster inference speeds through optimized parameter allocations and knowledge distillation techniques.
cot_prompt: Recent studies reveal that while non-autoregressive models offer efficiency, they can achieve competitive performance by leveraging stronger autoregressive architectures, demonstrating significant improvements over previous approaches in terms of both speed and accuracy.
dsp_prompt: Recent studies comparing non-autoregressive and autoregressive neural machine translation highlight the potential for significantly faster inference speeds using deep encoder architectures while maintaining competitive performance, challenging assumptions about the computational efficiency and accuracy trade-offs between approaches.

titles: Mincut Pooling in Graph Neural Networks
keywords: Graph Neural Networks; Pooling; Graph Cuts; Spectral Clustering
abstracts:
The advance of node pooling operations in Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) has lagged behind the feverish design of new message-passing techniques, and pooling remains an important and challenging endeavor for the design of deep architectures.
In this paper, we propose a pooling operation for GNNs that leverages a differentiable unsupervised loss based on the minCut optimization objective.
For each node, our method learns a soft cluster assignment vector that depends on the node features, the target inference task (e.g., a graph classification loss), and, thanks to the minCut objective, also on the connectivity structure of the graph.
Graph pooling is obtained by applying the matrix of assignment vectors to the adjacency matrix and the node features.
We validate the effectiveness of the proposed pooling method on a variety of supervised and unsupervised tasks.
one_sentence_summary: A new pooling layer for GNNs that learns how to pool nodes, according to their features, the graph connectivity, and the dowstream task objective.
standard_prompt: Our study introduces MinCUT-based node pooling in Graph Neural Networks, enhancing clustering accuracy with a novel differentiable loss function optimized via minCut theory, demonstrating its utility across various tasks including both supervised and unsupervised learning scenarios.
cot_prompt: The authors introduce MinCutPooling, a differentiable pooling operation for Graph Neural Networks designed to optimize a minimization problem using the minCut criterion, thereby enhancing the performance of node representations across various tasks.
dsp_prompt: Our work introduces a novel pooling mechanism within Graph Neural Networks that utilizes the min-cut optimization to dynamically assign nodes into clusters, thereby enhancing both the efficiency and accuracy of feature extraction across various tasks.

titles: LMSYS-Chat-1M: A Large-Scale Real-World LLM Conversation Dataset
keywords: large language models; dataset; conversation; safety; benchmark
abstracts: Studying how people interact with large language models (LLMs) in real-world scenarios is increasingly important due to their widespread use in various applications. In this paper, we introduce LMSYS-Chat-1M, a large-scale dataset containing one million real-world conversations with 25 state-of-the-art LLMs. This dataset is collected from 210K unique IP addresses in the wild on our Vicuna demo and Chatbot Arena website. We offer an overview of the dataset's content, including its curation process, basic statistics, and topic distribution, highlighting its diversity, originality, and scale. We demonstrate its versatility through four use cases: developing content moderation models that perform similarly to GPT-4, building a safety benchmark, training instruction-following models that perform similarly to Vicuna, and creating challenging benchmark questions. We believe that this dataset will serve as a valuable resource for understanding and advancing LLM capabilities. The dataset is publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/lmsys/lmsys-chat-1m.
one_sentence_summary: This paper introduces LMSYS-Chat-1M, a large-scale dataset containing one million real-world conversations with 25 state-of-the-art LLMs.
standard_prompt: The LMSYS-Chat-1M dataset contains one million real-world conversations between 25 state-of-the-art LLMs, offering insights into LLM behavior and potential application areas.
cot_prompt: LMSYS-Chat-1M introduces a large-scale real-world conversation dataset containing over one million interactions between users and 25 leading LLMs, offering diverse insights into LLM performance across multiple applications.
dsp_prompt: The LMSYS-Chat-1M dataset contains one million real-world conversations between 25 state-of-the-art LLMs, providing diverse, original, and scalable data for studying LLM capabilities across multiple use cases.

titles: Near-optimal Coresets for Robust Clustering
keywords: clustering; outlier; robustness; coreset
abstracts: We consider robust clustering problems in $\mathbb{R}^d$, specifically $k$-clustering problems (e.g., $k$-Median and $k$-Means) with $m$ \emph{outliers}, where the cost for a given center set $C \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ aggregates the distances from $C$ to all but the furthest $m$ data points, instead of all points as in classical clustering. We focus on the $\epsilon$-coreset for robust clustering, a small proxy of the dataset that preserves the clustering cost within $\epsilon$-relative error for all center sets. Our main result is an $\epsilon$-coreset of size $O(m + \mathrm{poly}(k \epsilon^{-1}))$ that can be constructed in near-linear time. This significantly improves previous results, which either suffers an exponential dependence on $(m + k)$ [Feldman and Schulman, SODA'12], or has a weaker bi-criteria guarantee [Huang et al., FOCS'18]. Furthermore, we show this dependence in $m$ is nearly-optimal, and the fact that it is isolated from other factors may be crucial for dealing with large number of outliers. We construct our coresets by adapting to the outlier setting a recent framework [Braverman et al., FOCS'22] which was designed for capacity-constrained clustering, overcoming a new challenge that the participating terms in the cost, particularly the excluded $m$ outlier points, are dependent on the center set $C$. We validate our coresets on various datasets, and we observe a superior size-accuracy tradeoff compared with popular baselines including uniform sampling and sensitivity sampling. We also achieve a significant speedup of existing approximation algorithms for robust clustering using our coresets.
one_sentence_summary: We obtain an \epsilon-coreset of near-optimal size for (k, z)-clustering (which includes k-median and k-means) with m outliers
standard_prompt: Our work introduces an efficient $\epsilon$-coreset construction algorithm for robust clustering, achieving a size-dependent bound of $O(m + \mathrm{poly}(k \epsilon^{-1}))$ while maintaining accuracy within $\epsilon$ relative error, thereby improving upon previous approaches and enabling faster computation even when dealing with a large number of outliers.
cot_prompt: Our work introduces an efficient $\epsilon$-coreset construction algorithm for robust clustering, achieving a nearly optimal size-accuracy trade-off while constructing coresets of size $O(m + \mathrm{poly}(k \epsilon^{-1}))$ for $k$-clustering problems, significantly improving upon previous methods in both efficiency and accuracy.
dsp_prompt: We introduce an efficient $\epsilon$-coreset construction method for robust $k$-clustering with $m$ outliers, achieving a size-independent dependence on $m+k$ while maintaining $\epsilon$-approximation guarantees, demonstrating improved performance over existing methods on both accuracy and efficiency metrics.

titles: Penetrating the Fog: the Path to Efficient CNN Models
keywords: Efficient CNN models; Computer Vision
abstracts: With the increasing demand to deploy convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on mobile platforms, the sparse kernel approach was proposed, which could save more parameters than the standard convolution while maintaining accuracy. However, despite the great potential, no prior research has pointed out how to craft an sparse kernel design with such potential (i.e., effective design), and all prior works just adopt simple combinations of existing sparse kernels such as group convolution. Meanwhile due to the large design space it is also impossible to try all combinations of existing sparse kernels. In this paper, we are the first in the field to consider how to craft an effective sparse kernel design by eliminating the large design space. Specifically, we present a sparse kernel scheme to illustrate how to reduce the space from three aspects. First, in terms of composition we remove designs composed of repeated layers. Second, to remove designs with large accuracy degradation, we find an unified property named~\emph{information field} behind various sparse kernel designs, which could directly indicate the final accuracy. Last, we remove designs in two cases where a better parameter efficiency could be achieved. Additionally, we provide detailed efficiency analysis on the final 4 designs in our scheme. Experimental results validate the idea of our scheme by showing that our scheme is able to find designs which are more efficient in using parameters and computation with similar or higher accuracy.
one_sentence_summary: We are the first in the field to show how to craft an effective sparse kernel design from three aspects: composition, performance and efficiency.
standard_prompt: Our study introduces a novel method for designing sparse kernels through compositional optimization, identifying key properties like "information fields," and efficiently reduces the search space, ultimately leading to more efficient convolutional neural network models.
cot_prompt: Our work introduces a novel method for crafting effective sparse kernel designs through compositional elimination, accurate evaluation of information fields, and targeted optimization, demonstrating improved parameter efficiency and comparable/higher accuracy across four distinct schemes.
dsp_prompt: Our study introduces a novel sparse kernel design method for CNNs, significantly reducing the search space and improving parameter efficiency while preserving network accuracy through compositional removal, accurate degradation detection, and optimal parameter allocation strategies.

titles: Generalized Domain Adaptation with Covariate and Label Shift CO-ALignment
keywords: Domain Adaptation; Label Shift; Covariate Shift
abstracts: Unsupervised knowledge transfer has a great potential to improve the generalizability of deep models to novel domains. Yet the current literature assumes that the label distribution is domain-invariant and only aligns the covariate or vice versa. In this paper, we explore the task of Generalized Domain Adaptation (GDA): How to transfer knowledge across different domains in the presence of both covariate and label shift? We propose a covariate and label distribution CO-ALignment (COAL) model to tackle this problem. Our model leverages prototype-based conditional alignment and label distribution estimation to diminish the covariate and label shifts, respectively. We demonstrate experimentally that when both types of shift exist in the data, COAL leads to state-of-the-art performance on several cross-domain benchmarks.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a covariate and label distribution CO-ALignment (COAL) model to tackle Generalized Domain Adaptation (GDA) with covariant shift and label shift.
standard_prompt: In this study, the authors introduce the CO-ALignment (Covariate and Label Distribution Alignment) model for generalized domain adaptation, which addresses the challenge of transferring knowledge across domains while accounting for both covariate and label shifts through prototype-based conditional alignment and label distribution estimation.
cot_prompt: The CO-ALignment model addresses the challenge of generalized domain adaptation by jointly mitigating covariate and label shifts through prototype-based conditional alignment and label distribution estimation, achieving superior results across various cross-domain datasets.
dsp_prompt: In this study, the authors introduce a CO-ALignment (covariate and label distribution alignment) model for generalized domain adaptation, which effectively mitigates both covariate and label shifts through prototype-based conditional alignment and label distribution estimation, achieving superior performance on cross-domain tasks.

titles: TPE: Towards Better Compositional Reasoning over Conceptual Tools with Multi-persona Collaboration
keywords: Tool Learning; Dialogue System; Large Language Models
abstracts: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated exceptional performance in planning the use of various **functional tools** in question-answering, such as calculators and retrievers. In this paper, we first broaden the scope of the tool, centered around **conceptual tools** in the context of dialogue systems. A **conceptual tool** specifies a cognitive concept used to help systematic or investigative thought. Such **conceptual tools** play key roles in practice, such as multiple psychological / tutoring strategies being dynamically applied in a single turn to compose helpful responses. To further enhance the reasoning and planning capability of LLMs over these **conceptual tools**, we present a multi-persona collaboration framework: Think-Plan-Execute (*TPE*), which decouples the response generation process into three roles: thinker, planner, and executor. Specifically, the *Thinker* analyzes the internal status exhibited in the dialogue context, such as user emotions and preferences, to formulate a global guideline. The *Planner* generates executable plans to call different **conceptual tools** (a.k.a, different sources or strategies), while the *Executor* assembles all intermediate results into a coherent response. This structured approach enhances response explainability and controllability, reducing token redundancy simultaneously. We demonstrate the effectiveness of *TPE* across various dialogue response generation tasks, encompassing multi-source (FoCus) and multi-strategy interactions (CIMA and PsyQA), revealing its potential to address real-world dialogue interactions with the more complicated tool learning besides only **functional tools**. Full code and data will be released for reproduction.
one_sentence_summary: A novel multi-persona framework for LLMs to plan the use of conceptual tools in the context of dialogue systems
standard_prompt: A novel multi-persona collaboration framework, called Think-Plan-Execute (*TPE*), leverages conceptual tools in dialogue systems by breaking down response generation into thinking, planning, and executing phases, enhancing explanation and control while reducing redundancy and addressing real-world complexity beyond functional tools.
cot_prompt: The **TPE** framework combines **multi-persona collaboration** to enhance LLMs' reasoning over conceptual tools in dialogues, improving response quality and explainability through dynamic analysis, plan execution, and integration of diverse tools.
dsp_prompt: The Think-Plan-Execute (TPE) framework, leveraging conceptual tools and multi-persona collaboration, significantly enhances LLMs' compositional reasoning capabilities by structuring response generation into think, plan, and execute phases, thereby improving explanation, control, and versatility in handling diverse and complex tool interactions within dialogue systems.

titles: Graph Attention Networks
keywords: Deep Learning; Graph Convolutions; Attention; Self-Attention
abstracts: We present graph attention networks (GATs), novel neural network architectures that operate on graph-structured data, leveraging masked self-attentional layers to address the shortcomings of prior methods based on graph convolutions or their approximations. By stacking layers in which nodes are able to attend over their neighborhoods' features, we enable (implicitly) specifying different weights to different nodes in a neighborhood, without requiring any kind of computationally intensive matrix operation (such as inversion) or depending on knowing the graph structure upfront. In this way, we address several key challenges of spectral-based graph neural networks simultaneously, and make our model readily applicable to inductive as well as transductive problems. Our GAT models have achieved or matched state-of-the-art results across four established transductive and inductive graph benchmarks: the Cora, Citeseer and Pubmed citation network datasets, as well as a protein-protein interaction dataset (wherein test graphs remain unseen during training).
one_sentence_summary: A novel approach to processing graph-structured data by neural networks, leveraging attention over a node's neighborhood. Achieves state-of-the-art results on transductive citation network tasks and an inductive protein-protein interaction task.
standard_prompt: Graph attention networks leverage masked self-attentive layers to address limitations of existing graph neural network approaches by enabling flexible node weighting within local neighborhood interactions, enhancing performance across diverse graph tasks including both transductive and inductive learning scenarios.
cot_prompt: Graph attention networks leverage masked self-attentions to address limitations of previous graph convolutional approaches by enabling flexible node feature weighting without requiring matrix operations or prior knowledge of the graph structure.
dsp_prompt: Graph attention networks leverage masked self-attentional layers to address challenges in spectral-based graph neural networks by enabling implicit node feature weighting and making them suitable for both transductive and inductive learning tasks.

titles: Optimistic Exploration even with a Pessimistic Initialisation
keywords: Reinforcement Learning; Exploration; Optimistic Initialisation
abstracts: Optimistic initialisation is an effective strategy for efficient exploration in reinforcement learning (RL). In the tabular case, all provably efficient model-free algorithms rely on it. However, model-free deep RL algorithms do not use optimistic initialisation despite taking inspiration from these provably efficient tabular algorithms. In particular, in scenarios with only positive rewards, Q-values are initialised at their lowest possible values due to commonly used network initialisation schemes, a pessimistic initialisation. Merely initialising the network to output optimistic Q-values is not enough, since we cannot ensure that they remain optimistic for novel state-action pairs, which is crucial for exploration. We propose a simple count-based augmentation to pessimistically initialised Q-values that separates the source of optimism from the neural network. We show that this scheme is provably efficient in the tabular setting and extend it to the deep RL setting. Our algorithm, Optimistic Pessimistically Initialised Q-Learning (OPIQ), augments the Q-value estimates of a DQN-based agent with count-derived bonuses to ensure optimism during both action selection and bootstrapping. We show that OPIQ outperforms non-optimistic DQN variants that utilise a pseudocount-based intrinsic motivation in hard exploration tasks, and that it predicts optimistic estimates for novel state-action pairs.
one_sentence_summary: We augment the Q-value estimates with a count-based bonus that ensures optimism during action selection and bootstrapping, even if the Q-value estimates are pessimistic.
standard_prompt: In the tabular setting, merely optimistically initializing Q-values is insufficient for maintaining optimism; hence, we introduce a count-based augmentation to pessimistically initialized Q-values in Deep Reinforcement Learning, achieving significant performance improvements over non-optimistic approaches.
cot_prompt: In reinforcement learning, optimistically initializing Q-values can lead to poor exploration, but using a count-based augmentation to separate optimism from the network ensures better performance in challenging scenarios.
dsp_prompt: Optimistic Pessimistic Initialisation (OPI) enhances reinforcement learning agents' exploration by separating optimism from neural networks through a count-based augmentation, leading to superior performance in high-exploration tasks.

titles: Continual Momentum Filtering on Parameter Space for Online Test-time Adaptation
keywords: Online Test-time Adaptation; Catastrophic Forgetting; Kalman Filter
abstracts: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have revolutionized tasks such as image classification and speech recognition but often falter when training and test data diverge in distribution. External factors, from weather effects on images to varied speech environments, can cause this discrepancy, compromising DNN performance. Online test-time adaptation (OTTA) methods present a promising solution, recalibrating models in real-time during the test stage without requiring historical data. However, the OTTA paradigm is imperfect, often falling prey to issues such as catastrophic forgetting due to its reliance on noisy, self-trained predictions. Although some contemporary strategies mitigate this by tying adaptations to the static source model, this restricts model flexibility. This paper introduces a continual momentum filtering (CMF) framework, leveraging the Kalman filter (KF) to strike a balance between model adaptability and information retention. The CMF intertwines optimization via stochastic gradient descent with a KF-based inference process. This methodology not only aids in averting catastrophic forgetting but also provides high adaptability to shifting data distributions. We validate our framework on various OTTA scenarios and real-world situations regarding covariate and label shifts, and the CMF consistently shows superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.
one_sentence_summary: We propose continual momentum filtering framework, which a novel approach to bolster the online test-time adaptation methodology. This was achieved by deducing a refined source model through target model denoising by leveraging the Kalman filtering.
standard_prompt: The Continual Momentum Filtering (CMF) framework combines online test-time adaptation techniques with the Kalman Filter to address catastrophic forgetting while maintaining high adaptability to varying data distributions through a novel approach that integrates stochastic gradient descent with KF-based inference.
cot_prompt: The Continual Momentum Filtering (CMF) framework, combining Kalman filter-based inference with stochastic gradient descent, addresses the issue of catastrophic forgetting in online test-time adaptation through a novel method that strikes a balance between model flexibility and information retention, demonstrating superior performance across different types of data shifts.
dsp_prompt: The continual momentum filtering framework, combining stochastic gradient descent and Kalman filter inference, offers robust online test-time adaptation in deep learning, mitigating catastrophic forgetting while maintaining high flexibility through dynamic parameter updates.

titles: Efficient Content-Based Sparse Attention with Routing Transformers
keywords: Sparse attention; autoregressive; generative models
abstracts:
Self-attention has recently been adopted for a wide range of sequence modeling
problems. Despite its effectiveness, self-attention suffers quadratic compute and
memory requirements with respect to sequence length. Successful approaches to
reduce this complexity focused on attention to local sliding windows or a small
set of locations independent of content. Our work proposes to learn dynamic
sparse attention patterns that avoid allocating computation and memory to attend
to content unrelated to the query of interest. This work builds upon two lines of
research: it combines the modeling flexibility of prior work on content-based sparse
attention with the efficiency gains from approaches based on local, temporal sparse
attention. Our model, the Routing Transformer, endows self-attention with a sparse
routing module based on online k-means while reducing the overall complexity of
attention to O(n^{1.5}d) from O(n^2d) for sequence length n and hidden dimension
d. We show that our model outperforms comparable sparse attention models on
language modeling on Wikitext-103 (15.8 vs 18.3 perplexity) as well as on
image generation on ImageNet-64 (3.43 vs 3.44 bits/dim) while using fewer self-attention layers.
Code will be open-sourced on acceptance.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a content-based sparse attention model and show improvements on language modeling and image generation.
standard_prompt: The Routing Transformer combines the benefits of content-based sparse attention with reduced computational complexity through an online k-means-based routing mechanism, achieving superior performance on language modeling tasks compared to traditional methods while minimizing self-attention layer usage.
cot_prompt: The Routing Transformer combines the benefits of content-based sparse attention with efficient self-attention mechanisms, achieving reduced computational complexity and better performance on language modeling tasks compared to previous methods.
dsp_prompt: The Routing Transformer combines the benefits of content-aware sparse attention with efficient self-attention mechanisms, achieving linear time complexity for long sequences and superior performance across language modeling tasks while using fewer parameters.

titles: MVP: Multi-task Supervised Pre-training for Natural Language Generation
keywords: Natural language generation; pretrained language models; multi-task learning; prompt learning
abstracts: Pre-trained language models (PLMs) have achieved remarkable success in natural language generation (NLG) tasks. Up to now, most NLG-oriented PLMs are pre-trained in an unsupervised manner using the large-scale general corpus. In the meanwhile, an increasing number of models pre-trained with labeled data (i.e., “supervised pre-training”) showcase superior performance compared to unsupervised pre-trained models. Motivated by the success of supervised pre-training, we propose Multi-task superVised Pre-training (MVP) for natural language generation. We collect a large-scale natural language generation corpus, MVPCorpus, from $77$ datasets over $11$ diverse NLG tasks. Then we unify these examples into a general text-to-text format to pre-train the text generation model MVP in a supervised manner. For each task, we further pre-train specific soft prompts to stimulate the model’s capacity to perform a specific task. Extensive experiments have demonstrated the effectiveness and generalizability of our MVP model in a number of NLG tasks, which achieves state-of-the-art performance on $13$ out of $17$ datasets.
one_sentence_summary: We pre-train a model MVP and task-specific prompts for natural language generation tasks with our collected labeled corpora MVPCorpus.
standard_prompt: Multi-task supervised pre-training (MVP) leverages a large-scale dataset of diverse natural language generation tasks to train a unified text-to-text model, achieving state-of-the-art performance across multiple NLP applications.
cot_prompt: Multi-task Supervised Pre-training (MVP) leverages both large-scale general corpora and labeled data to effectively train a unified text-to-text model across multiple natural language generation tasks, achieving state-of-the-art performance on various datasets.
dsp_prompt: The proposed MVP model, unified through a large-scale dataset, utilizes supervised pre-training techniques to enhance its ability across various natural language generation tasks, achieving significant improvements in performance across multiple datasets.

titles: Modeling label correlations implicitly through latent label encodings for multi-label text classification
keywords: multi-label text classification; multi-label classification; label correlation; label embedding
abstracts: Multi-label text classification (MLTC) aims to assign a set of labels to each given document. Unlike single-label text classification methods that often focus on document representation learning, MLTC faces a key challenge of modeling label correlations due to complex label dependencies. Previous state-of-the-art works model label correlations explicitly. It lacks flexibility and is prone to introduce inductive bias that may not always hold, such as label-correlation simplification, sequencing label sets, and label-correlation overload. To address this issue, this paper uses latent label representations to model label correlations implicitly. Specifically, the proposed method concatenates a set of latent labels (instead of actual labels) to the text tokens, inputs them to BERT, then maps the contextual encodings of these latent labels to actual labels cooperatively. The correlations between labels, and between labels and the text are modeled indirectly through these latent-label  encodings and their correlations. Such latent and distributed correlation modeling can impose less a priori limits and provide more flexibility. The method is conceptually simple but quite effective. It improves the state-of-the-art results on two widely used benchmark datasets by a large margin. Further experiments demonstrate that its effectiveness lies in label-correlation utilization rather than document representation. Feature study reveals the importance of using latent label embeddings. It also reveals that contrary to the other token embeddings, the embeddings of these latent labels are sensitive to tasks; sometimes pretraining them can lead to significant performance loss rather than promotion. This result suggests that they are more related to task information (i.e., the actual labels) than the other tokens.
one_sentence_summary: It is the first method to model label-correlations implicitly for multi-label text classification to our knowledge, it has outperformed the state-of-the-art results on two widelly used datasets by a large margin.
standard_prompt: This paper proposes a novel approach to implicitly model label correlations in multi-label text classification by utilizing latent label encodings, which allows for flexible and accurate labeling based on complex label dependencies, outperforming existing methods on standard benchmarks.
cot_prompt: This paper proposes a novel implicit model for multi-label text classification by utilizing latent label representations, which effectively models label correlations and improves upon previous approaches by reducing complexity and enhancing flexibility while maintaining high accuracy.
dsp_prompt: This paper proposes a novel approach to implicitly model label correlations in multi-label text classification by utilizing latent label representations, which significantly outperforms existing methods while maintaining conceptual simplicity and demonstrating sensitivity to specific tasks.

titles: Robust Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks
keywords: conditional GAN; unsupervised pathway; autoencoder; robustness
abstracts: Conditional generative adversarial networks (cGAN) have led to large improvements in the task of conditional image generation, which lies at the heart of computer vision. The major focus so far has been on performance improvement, while there has been little effort in making cGAN more robust to noise. The regression (of the generator) might lead to arbitrarily large errors in the output, which makes cGAN unreliable for real-world applications. In this work, we introduce a novel conditional GAN model, called RoCGAN, which leverages structure in the target space of the model to address the issue. Our model augments the generator with an unsupervised pathway, which promotes the outputs of the generator to span the target manifold even in the presence of intense noise. We prove that RoCGAN share similar theoretical properties as GAN and experimentally verify that our model outperforms existing state-of-the-art cGAN architectures by a large margin in a variety of domains including images from natural scenes and faces.
one_sentence_summary: We introduce a new type of conditional GAN, which aims to leverage structure in the target space of the generator. We augment the generator with a new, unsupervised pathway to learn the target structure.
standard_prompt: RoCGAN, an innovative conditional GAN architecture, addresses the limitations of traditional cGAN by incorporating an unsupervised pathway that enhances the generative process's ability to maintain accuracy despite noisy inputs, leading to superior performance across various domains compared to other models.
cot_prompt: RoCGAN, an improved version of the Conditional Generative Adversarial Network, enhances the reliability of conditional image generation through a structured augmentation of the generator's outputs, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing methods across diverse datasets.
dsp_prompt: Our novel conditional GAN architecture, RoCGAN, introduces a structured representation to enhance the robustness and reliability of generator outputs, particularly in the presence of noise, thereby significantly improving its performance across various domains compared to existing methods.

titles: MobileBERT: Task-Agnostic Compression of BERT by Progressive Knowledge Transfer
keywords: BERT; knowledge transfer; model compression
abstracts: The recent development of Natural Language Processing (NLP) has achieved great success using large pre-trained models with hundreds of millions of parameters. However, these models suffer from the heavy model size and high latency such that we cannot directly deploy them to resource-limited mobile devices. In this paper, we propose MobileBERT for compressing and accelerating the popular BERT model. Like BERT, MobileBERT is task-agnostic; that is, it can be universally applied to various downstream NLP tasks via fine-tuning. MobileBERT is a slimmed version of BERT-LARGE augmented with bottleneck structures and a carefully designed balance between self-attentions and feed-forward networks. To train MobileBERT, we use a bottom-to-top progressive scheme to transfer the intrinsic knowledge of a specially designed Inverted Bottleneck BERT-LARGE teacher to it. Empirical studies show that MobileBERT is 4.3x smaller and 4.0x faster than original BERT-BASE while achieving competitive results on well-known NLP benchmarks. On the natural language inference tasks of GLUE, MobileBERT achieves 0.6 GLUE score performance degradation, and 367 ms latency on a Pixel 3 phone. On the SQuAD v1.1/v2.0 question answering task, MobileBERT achieves a 90.0/79.2 dev F1 score, which is 1.5/2.1 higher than BERT-BASE.
one_sentence_summary: We develop a task-agnosticlly compressed BERT, which is 4.3x smaller and 4.0x faster than BERT-BASE while achieving competitive performance on GLUE and SQuAD.
standard_prompt: MobileBERT is a lightweight variant of BERT-LARGE, specifically optimized for mobile applications through a progressive knowledge transfer approach, demonstrating significant efficiency gains over the full-sized BERT model while maintaining comparable performance across various NLP tasks.
cot_prompt: MobileBERT, a task-agnostic compression method, significantly reduces the size and increases the speed of BERT, achieving up to 4.3 times smaller and 4.0 times faster computational efficiency compared to its original version, specifically outperforming BERT-BASE across multiple NLP tasks including natural language inference and question answering, demonstrating substantial improvements in both computational resources and accuracy on mobile devices.
dsp_prompt: MobileBERT is a lightweight variant of BERT that leverages knowledge transfer through a progressive approach, significantly reducing its size and improving speed while maintaining comparable performance across various NLP tasks, making it highly effective for deploying large-scale NLP models on resource-constrained mobile devices.

titles: Text2NKG: Fine-Grained N-ary Relation Extraction for N-ary relational Knowledge Graph Construction
keywords: N-ary Relation Extraction; N-ary relational Knowledge Graph; Knowledge Graph Construction
abstracts: Beyond traditional binary relational facts, n-ary relational knowledge graphs (NKGs) are comprised of n-ary relational facts containing more than two entities, which are closer to real-world facts with broader applications. However, the construction of NKGs still significantly relies on manual labor, and n-ary relation extraction still remains at a course-grained level, which is always in a single schema and fixed arity of entities. To address these restrictions, we propose Text2NKG, a novel fine-grained n-ary relation extraction framework for n-ary relational knowledge graph construction. We introduce a span-tuple classification approach with hetero-ordered merging to accomplish fine-grained n-ary relation extraction in different arity. Furthermore, Text2NKG supports four typical NKG schemas: hyper-relational schema, event-based schema, role-based schema, and hypergraph-based schema, with high flexibility and practicality. Experimental results demonstrate that Text2NKG outperforms the previous state-of-the-art model by nearly 20\% points in the $F_1$ scores on the fine-grained n-ary relation extraction benchmark in the hyper-relational schema. Our code and datasets are publicly available.
one_sentence_summary: We introduce Text2NKG, a novel fine-grained n-ary relation extraction framework for n-ary relational knowledge graph construction.
standard_prompt: Text2NKG, an innovative fine-grained n-ary relation extraction framework, leverages a span-tuple classification approach with hetero-ordered merging and supports multiple NKG schemas, achieving significant improvements over existing methods in the F1 score benchmark, particularly in the hyper-relational schema.
cot_prompt: Text2NKG, an innovative text-to-nary knowledge graph conversion system, introduces a span-tuple classification method with heterogeneous merging to achieve fine-grained n-ary relation extraction across various schemas, demonstrating superior performance over existing models in specific domains.
dsp_prompt: Text2NKG, an innovative text-to-nary-knowledge-graph framework, leverages a span-tuple classification approach with heterogeneous ordering and merging to achieve fine-grained n-ary relation extraction across diverse schema types, showcasing significant improvements over existing methods in both accuracy and flexibility.

titles: Learned optimizers that outperform on wall-clock and validation loss
keywords: Learned Optimizers; Meta-Learning
abstracts: Deep learning has shown that learned functions can dramatically outperform hand-designed functions on perceptual tasks. Analogously, this suggests that learned update functions may similarly outperform current hand-designed optimizers, especially for specific tasks. However, learned optimizers are notoriously difficult to train and have yet to demonstrate wall-clock speedups over hand-designed optimizers, and thus are rarely used in practice. Typically, learned optimizers are trained by truncated backpropagation through an unrolled optimization process.
