On the other hand, training-free methods such as universal guidance, though more flexible, have yet to demonstrate comparable performance. 
In this work, through a comprehensive investigation into the design space, we show that it is possible to achieve significant performance improvements over existing guidance schemes by leveraging off-the-shelf classifiers in a training-free fashion, enjoying the best of both worlds. 
Employing calibration as a general guideline, we propose several pre-conditioning techniques to better exploit pretrained off-the-shelf classifiers for guiding diffusion generation. 
Extensive experiments on ImageNet validate our proposed method, showing that state-of-the-art (SOTA) diffusion models (DDPM, EDM, DiT) can be further improved (up to 20\%) using off-the-shelf classifiers with barely any extra computational cost.
With the proliferation of publicly available pretrained classifiers, our proposed approach has great potential and can be readily scaled up to text-to-image generation tasks.
one_sentence_summary: Through a comprehensive investigation into the design space of classifier guidance in diffusion generation, we achieved significant improvements over existing guidance schemes by leveraging off-the-shelf classifiers in a training-free fashion.
standard_prompt: The study explores how off-the-shelf classifiers can improve performance in classifier-guided diffusion generation by employing them as a pre-conditioner, leading to significant enhancements over existing methods while reducing computational costs significantly, demonstrating its practical utility across various image generation tasks including text-to-image synthesis.
cot_prompt: Guidance schemes for conditional diffusion generation often require labeled data or are computationally expensive. Leveraging off-the-shelf classifiers improves performance significantly in training-free methods, enhancing state-of-the-art diffusion models like DDPM, EDM, and DiT, achieving notable improvements while maintaining flexibility.
dsp_prompt: The study demonstrates that leveraging off-the-shelf classifiers in a training-free manner significantly improves classification-guided diffusion generation, achieving notable performance enhancements compared to existing approaches while maintaining low computational overhead.

titles: XGAN: Unsupervised Image-to-Image Translation for many-to-many Mappings
keywords: unsupervised; gan; domain adaptation; style transfer; semantic; image translation; dataset
abstracts: Style transfer usually refers to the task of applying color and texture information from a specific style image to a given content image while preserving the structure of the latter. Here we tackle the more generic problem of semantic style transfer: given two unpaired collections of images, we aim to learn a mapping between the corpus-level style of each collection, while preserving semantic content shared across the two domains. We introduce XGAN ("Cross-GAN"), a dual adversarial autoencoder, which captures a shared representation of the common domain semantic content in an unsupervised way, while jointly learning the domain-to-domain image translations in both directions.  We exploit ideas from the domain adaptation literature and define a semantic consistency loss which encourages the model to preserve semantics in the learned embedding space. We report promising qualitative results for the task of face-to-cartoon translation. The cartoon dataset we collected for this purpose will also be released as a new benchmark for semantic style transfer.
one_sentence_summary: XGAN is an unsupervised model for feature-level image-to-image translation applied to semantic style transfer problems such as the face-to-cartoon task, for which we introduce a new dataset.
standard_prompt: XGAN, an unsupervised dual adversarial autoencoder, learns shared representations of cross-dataset semantic content while optimizing a domain-specific loss function, demonstrating successful face-to-cartoon translation.
cot_prompt: XGAN introduces an unsupervised dual adversarial autoencoder framework that learns shared representations for cross-dataset semantic styles, achieving promising face-to-cartoon translation results with a novel cartoon dataset release.
dsp_prompt: XGAN introduces a dual adversarial autoencoder framework to achieve cross-domain image translation by capturing shared semantic representations during unsupervised training, demonstrating its effectiveness through successful face-to-cartoon style transfer applications.

titles: Natural Language Adversarial Attack and Defense in Word Level
keywords: adversarial examples; text adversarial defense; text adversarial attack; synonym encoding; natural language processing
abstracts: Up until very recently, inspired by a mass of researches on adversarial examples for computer vision, there has been a growing interest in designing adversarial attacks for Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks, followed by very few works of adversarial defenses for NLP. To our knowledge, there exists no defense method against the successful synonym substitution based attacks that aim to satisfy all the lexical, grammatical, semantic constraints and thus are hard to perceived by humans. We contribute to fill this gap and propose a novel adversarial defense method called Synonym Encoding Method (SEM), which inserts an encoder before the input layer of the model and then trains the model to eliminate adversarial perturbations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SEM can efficiently defend current best synonym substitution based adversarial attacks with little decay on the accuracy for benign examples. To better evaluate SEM, we also design a strong attack method called Improved Genetic Algorithm (IGA) that adopts the genetic metaheuristic for synonym substitution based attacks. Compared with existing genetic based adversarial attack, IGA can achieve higher attack success rate while maintaining the transferability of the adversarial examples.
one_sentence_summary: The first text adversarial defense method in word level, and the improved generic based attack method against synonyms substitution based attacks.
standard_prompt: The Novel Synonym Encoding Method (SEM) introduces an encoder before the input layer of neural networks to effectively mitigate adversarial attacks targeting synonym substitutions, achieving superior performance over both traditional methods like improved genetic algorithms (IGA) and previous adversarial defenses in preserving model accuracy despite being effective at defending against specific types of synonym-based attacks.
cot_prompt: The Novel Synonym Encoding Method (SEM) combines an encoder with adversarial training to effectively defend against current best synonym substitution-based adversarial attacks in natural language processing, achieving high robustness compared to both traditional defenses and state-of-the-art genetic-based attacks.
dsp_prompt: The Novel Synonym Encoding Method (SEM) addresses the challenge of defending against synonym substitution-based adversarial attacks in natural language processing (NLP) by inserting an encoder into the model and training it to remove adversarial perturbations, demonstrating effective performance in both benign and adversarial scenarios.

titles: $L_q$ regularization for Fairness AI robust to sampling bias
keywords: Fairness AI; Sampling bias; Robustness
abstracts: It is well recognized that historical biases exist in training data against a certain sensitive group (e.g., non-white, women) which are socially unacceptable, and these unfair biases are inherited to trained AI models. Various learning algorithms have been proposed to remove or alleviate unfair biases in trained AI models. In this paper, we consider another type of bias in training data so-called {\it sampling bias} in view of fairness AI. Here, sampling bias means that training data do not represent well the population of interest. Sampling bias occurs when special sampling designs (e.g., stratified sampling) are used when collecting training data, or the population where training data are collected is different from the population of interest. When sampling bias exists, fair AI models on training data may not be fair in test data. To ensure fairness on test data, we develop computationally efficient learning algorithms robust to sampling bias. In particular, we propose a robust fairness constraint based on the $L_q$ norm which is a generic algorithm to be applied to various fairness AI problems without much hamper. By analyzing multiple benchmark data sets, we show that our proposed robust fairness AI algorithm improves existing fair AI algorithms much in terms of the robustness to sampling bias and has significant computational advantages compared to other robust fair AI algorithms.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a robust fairness constraint based on the Lq norm which is robust to sampling bias, computationally efficient and can be easily applied to various fairness AI problems.
standard_prompt: We propose a novel $L_q$ regularization approach to enhance fairness in artificial intelligence models by addressing sampling bias, leading to improved accuracy and efficiency over traditional fairness constraints.
cot_prompt: The study introduces a new robust fairness constraint using $L_q$ regularization, demonstrating improved performance over existing methods by mitigating bias due to sampling design, making it effective for various fairness AI applications with enhanced computational efficiency.
dsp_prompt: We introduce a novel $L_q$ regularized approach for enhancing fairness in artificial intelligence by addressing sampling bias in training data, demonstrating superior performance over existing methods in terms of both fairness and efficiency.

titles: Achieving Certified Robustness and Maintaining Clean Accuracy via Vanilla Model Guide
keywords: Adversarial examples; Certified Robustness
abstracts:
Certified robustness can provide theoretical defense guarantees for deep neural network models against adversarial examples within a certain perturbation range. However, existing research on obtaining certified robustness requires specialized certified robust training from scratch for DNNs models. This approach significantly decreases the clean accuracy of normal inputs compared to vanilla models trained with vanilla training, affecting the main inference task of DNNs models and causing practical difficulties for security methods.
We propose a practical training method that aims to obtain certified robustness while maintaining clean accuracy.
This method involves adding a pre-trained vanilla model and applying singular value decomposition (SVD) to the weight matrices of each network layer of the vanilla model. This process yields rotation matrices and singular values that respectively affect clean accuracy and certified robustness. The vanilla model is used as a guide model, establishing a knowledge transfer process based on the similarity of rotation matrices between the guide model and the certification model that obtains certified robustness. In order to select important rotation matrix information and reduce computational cost, a low-rank approximation is used for practical knowledge transfer. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly improves clean accuracy while only slightly reducing certified accuracy.
one_sentence_summary: With the help of pre-trained vanilla model guidance improves the model's ability to represent clean inputs in certified robust training.
standard_prompt: Our novel method integrates a pre-trained vanilla model as a guide, using SVD to derive rotation matrices and singular values, which helps maintain clean accuracy while achieving certified robustness through knowledge transfer.
cot_prompt: Our novel training method enhances certified robustness by leveraging a pre-trained vanilla model, using SVD for weight transformations, and transferring knowledge through low-rank approximations to maintain clean accuracy while achieving improved defense capabilities.
dsp_prompt: Our proposed method combines a pre-trained vanilla model as a guide, using SVD to extract rotation matrices and singular values, which allows us to maintain clean accuracy while achieving certified robustness through knowledge transfer, demonstrating significant improvements over previous approaches.

titles: Sparse Token Transformer with Attention Back Tracking
keywords: Token Pruning; Sparse Token; Attention Back-tracking; BERT; Vision Transformer; DynamicViT
abstracts: Despite the success of Transformers in various applications from text, vision, and speech domains, they are yet to become standard architectures for mobile and edge device applications due to their heavy memory and computational requirements. While there exist many different approaches to reduce the complexities of the Transformers, such as the pruning of the weights/attentions/tokens, quantization, and distillation, we focus on token pruning, which reduces not only the complexity of the attention operations, but also the linear layers, which have non-negligible computational costs. However, previous token pruning approaches often remove tokens during the feed-forward stage without consideration of their impact on later layers' attentions, which has a potential risk of dropping out important tokens for the given task. To tackle this issue, we propose an attention back-tracking method that tracks the importance of each attention in a Transformer architecture from the outputs to the inputs, to preserve the tokens that have a large impact on the final predictions. We experimentally validate the effectiveness of the method on both NLP and CV benchmarks, using Transformer architectures for both domains, and the results show that the proposed attention back-tracking allows the model to better retain the full models' performance even at high sparsity rates, significantly outperforming all baselines. Qualitative analysis of the examples further shows that our method does preserve semantically meaningful tokens.
one_sentence_summary: We propose an attention back-tracking method that tracks the importance of each attention in a Transformer architecture from the outputs to the inputs, to preserve the tokens that have large impact on the final predictions.
standard_prompt: The Sparse Token Transformer with Attention Back-Tracking (SPTAB) introduces an attention back-tracking mechanism to improve the efficiency and accuracy of transformers by preserving critical tokens throughout the network's operation, demonstrating superior performance across multiple domains including natural language processing and computer vision.
cot_prompt: The Sparse Token Transformer with Attention Back-Tracking addresses the challenge of reducing the computational cost of Transformers by introducing an attention back-tracking mechanism that preserves critical tokens, leading to improved performance retention at high sparsity levels across natural language processing and computer vision tasks.
dsp_prompt: Our proposed attention back-tracking method enhances the effectiveness of sparse token pruning in transformers by tracking the importance of each attention operation across the entire network, allowing for more efficient model compression while maintaining critical semantic information.

titles: DreamSmooth: Improving Model-based Reinforcement Learning via Reward Smoothing
keywords: Model-based Reinforcement Learning; Reward Shaping; Reward Smoothing
abstracts: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) has gained much attention for its ability to learn complex behaviors in a sample-efficient way: planning actions by generating imaginary trajectories with predicted rewards. Despite its success, we found that surprisingly, reward prediction is often a bottleneck of MBRL, especially for sparse rewards that are challenging (or even ambiguous) to predict. Motivated by the intuition that humans can learn from rough reward estimates, we propose a simple yet effective reward smoothing approach, DreamSmooth, which learns to predict a temporally-smoothed reward, instead of the exact reward at the given timestep. We empirically show that DreamSmooth achieves state-of-the-art performance on long-horizon sparse-reward tasks both in sample efficiency and final performance without losing performance on common benchmarks, such as Deepmind Control Suite and Atari benchmarks.
one_sentence_summary: We show that reward prediction is challenging in many sparse-reward tasks, and propose a simple yet effective method, reward smoothing, which effectively facilitates reward prediction and thus, improves model-based reinforcement learning.
standard_prompt: DreamSmooth leverages temporal smoothing to enhance model-based reinforcement learning's robustness and efficiency, particularly for sparse rewards, achieving superior outcomes over traditional approaches in terms of sample efficiency and final performance across various benchmark tasks.
cot_prompt: DreamSmooth, an intuitive reward smoothing technique inspired by human behavior, significantly enhances model-based reinforcement learning's performance on sparse rewards across various benchmark tasks, demonstrating superior sample efficiency and final outcomes compared to traditional approaches.
dsp_prompt: DreamSmooth, an intuitive reward smoothing technique based on human learning insights, enhances model-based reinforcement learning's performance on sparse rewards by predicting smoothed rewards, achieving superior outcomes in terms of sample efficiency and final performance compared to traditional methods across various benchmark environments.

titles: Learning Similarity Metrics for Volumetric Simulations with Multiscale CNNs
keywords: metric learning; PDEs; numerical simulation; physical modeling
abstracts: Simulations that produce three-dimensional data are ubiquitous in science, ranging from fluid flows to plasma physics. We propose a similarity model based on entropy, which allows for the creation of physically meaningful ground truth distances for the similarity assessment of scalar and vectorial data, produced from transport and motion-based simulations. Utilizing two data acquisition methods derived from this model, we create collections of fields from numerical PDE solvers and existing simulation data repositories, and highlight the importance of an appropriate data distribution for an effective training process. Furthermore, a multiscale CNN architecture that computes a volumetric similarity metric (VolSiM) is proposed. To the best of our knowledge this is the first learning method inherently designed to address the challenges arising for the similarity assessment of high-dimensional simulation data. Additionally, the tradeoff between a large batch size and an accurate correlation computation for correlation-based loss functions is investigated, and the metric's equivariance with respect to rotation and scale operations is analyzed. Finally, the robustness and generalization of VolSiM is evaluated on a large range of test data, as well as a particularly challenging turbulence case study, that is close to potential real-world applications.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a learned metric for 3D data from numerical simulations that is motivated by an entropy-based similarity model.
standard_prompt: A novel learning framework, VolSiM, is introduced to assess the similarity of multidimensional simulation data using a multiscale convolutional neural network, addressing challenges such as large batch sizes and rotation/scale equivariance, and validated through extensive testing including both general performance evaluation and a specific turbulence analysis.
cot_prompt: A novel similarity metric called VolSiM, designed for volumetric simulation data, enhances efficient similarity assessments by leveraging a multiscale convolutional neural network, addressing batch size accuracy trade-offs, and demonstrating robustness across various datasets including turbulent conditions.
dsp_prompt: A novel similarity metric called VolSiM, based on an entropy model, is introduced to assess the similarity of high-dimensional simulation data using a multiscale convolutional neural network, addressing challenges such as batch size trade-offs and equivariance properties.

titles: Equal Improvability: A New Fairness Notion Considering the Long-term Impact
keywords: Fairness and Bias in Artificial Intelligence; Machine Learning
abstracts: Devising a fair classifier that does not discriminate against different groups is an important problem in machine learning. Although researchers have proposed various ways of defining group fairness, most of them only focused on the immediate fairness, ignoring the long-term impact of a fair classifier under the dynamic scenario where each individual can improve its feature over time. Such dynamic scenarios happen in real world, e.g., college admission and credit loaning, where each rejected sample makes effort to change its features to get accepted afterwards. In this dynamic setting, the long-term fairness should equalize the samples’ feature distribution across different groups after the rejected samples make some effort to improve. In order to promote long-term fairness, we propose a new fairness notion called Equal Improvability (EI), which equalizes the potential acceptance rate of the rejected samples across different groups assuming a bounded level of effort will be spent by each rejected sample. We analyze the properties of EI and its connections with existing fairness notions. To find a classifier that satisfies the EI requirement, we propose and study three different approaches that solve EI regularized optimization problems. Through experiments on both synthetic and real datasets, we demonstrate that the proposed EI-regularized algorithms encourage us to find a fair classifier in terms of EI. Finally, we provide experimental results on dynamic scenarios which highlight the advantages of our EI metric in achieving the long-term fairness. Codes are available in anonymous GitHub repository.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a new group fairness notion called Equal Improvability that equalizes the improvement of the rejected individuals across different groups.
standard_prompt: Equal Improvability is a novel fairness measure designed for classifiers that considers the long-term impact of improving features among rejected samples, promoting balanced outcomes even when individuals dynamically work to enhance their attributes.
cot_prompt: The authors introduce Equal Improvability (EI) as a novel measure for assessing long-term fairness in classification tasks, proposing three methods to achieve it and demonstrating its effectiveness through experiments on both synthetic and real data, showing improved performance in achieving long-term fairness compared to traditional fairness metrics.
dsp_prompt: Equal Improvability (EI) is a novel fairness concept designed to measure long-term fairness in classifiers, focusing on balancing current and future outcomes by considering the effort made by rejected samples, thereby promoting more equitable treatment over extended periods through optimized algorithmic fairness.

titles: Graph Edit Networks
keywords: graph neural networks; graph edit distance; time series prediction; structured prediction
abstracts: While graph neural networks have made impressive progress in classification and regression, few approaches to date perform time series prediction on graphs, and those that do are mostly limited to edge changes. We suggest that graph edits are a more natural interface for graph-to-graph learning. In particular,  graph edits are general enough to describe any graph-to-graph change, not only edge changes; they are sparse, making them easier to understand for humans and more efficient computationally; and they are local, avoiding the need for pooling layers in graph neural networks. In this paper, we propose a novel output layer - the graph edit network - which takes node embeddings as input and generates a sequence of graph edits that transform the input graph to the output graph. We prove that a mapping between the node sets of two graphs is sufficient to construct training data for a graph edit network and that an optimal mapping yields edit scripts that are almost as short as the graph edit distance between the graphs. We further provide a proof-of-concept empirical evaluation on several graph dynamical systems, which are difficult to learn for baselines from the literature.
one_sentence_summary: We show that graph neural networks can predict graph edits and are connected to the graph edit distance via graph mappings
standard_prompt: The authors introduce the Graph Edit Network (GEN), a new output layer for graph neural networks designed to efficiently capture graph transformations by generating sequences of minimal edits required to convert one graph into another, leveraging the GEN's ability to optimize mappings between nodes to enhance learning efficiency and accuracy in dynamic graph tasks.
cot_prompt: The authors introduce a novel output layer called the "graph edit network" that combines node embeddings with graph edits to efficiently predict graph transformations, demonstrating its effectiveness through empirical evaluations on challenging graph dynamic systems.
dsp_prompt: Graph edit networks, proposed as a novel output layer, offer a flexible and scalable approach to graph-to-graph transformations by leveraging sparse and localized edits, proving effective in both theory and practical applications across various dynamic graph datasets.

titles: Mitigating Memorization of Noisy Labels via Regularization between Representations
keywords: learning with noisy labels; representation learning
abstracts:
Designing robust loss functions is popular in learning with noisy labels while existing designs did not explicitly consider the overfitting property of deep neural networks (DNNs). As a result, applying these losses may still suffer from overfitting/memorizing noisy labels as training proceeds. In this paper, we first theoretically analyze the memorization effect and show that a lower-capacity model may perform better on noisy datasets. However, it is non-trivial to design a neural network with the best capacity given an arbitrary task. To circumvent this dilemma, instead of changing the model architecture, we decouple DNNs into an encoder followed by a linear classifier and propose to restrict the function space of a DNN by a representation regularizer. Particularly, we require the distance between two self-supervised features to be positively related to the distance between the corresponding two supervised model outputs.  
Our proposed framework is easily extendable and can incorporate many other robust loss functions to further improve performance. Extensive experiments and theoretical analyses support our claims. Code is available at https://github.com/UCSC-REAL/SelfSup_NoisyLabel.
one_sentence_summary: We theoretically show the memorization effect of DNN with resepct to the model capacity and propose a representation-based regularizer to mitigate the memorization effect.
standard_prompt: Designing a representation regularizer for self-supervised learning helps mitigate memorization of noisy labels by enforcing a positive relationship between self-supervised feature distances and supervised label distances, making it easier to train models that generalize well on noisy data.
cot_prompt: Designing a representation regularizer for DNNs helps mitigate memorization of noisy labels through optimizing feature distances between self-supervised and supervised representations.
dsp_prompt: Designing a representation regularizer for decoupled DNNs improves performance on noisy label learning by enforcing positive distances between self-supervised and supervised representations, effectively mitigating memorization issues through flexible incorporation of various robust loss functions.

titles: Learning Intuitive Policies Using Action Features
keywords: multi-agent coordination; attention; inductive bias
abstracts: An unaddressed challenge in multi-agent coordination is to enable AI agents to exploit the semantic relationships between the features of actions and the features of observations. Humans take advantage of these relationships in highly intuitive ways. For instance, in the absence of a shared language, we might point to the object we desire or hold up our fingers to indicate how many objects we want. To address this challenge, we investigate the effect of network architecture on the propensity of learning algorithms to exploit these semantic relationships. Across a procedurally generated coordination task, we find that attention-based architectures that jointly process a featurized representation of observations and actions have a better inductive bias for zero-shot coordination. Through fine-grained evaluation and scenario analysis, we show that the resulting policies are human-interpretable. Moreover, such agents coordinate with people without training on any human data.
one_sentence_summary: We show that certain network architectures encourage reinforcement learning algorithms to respect semantic relationships between actions and observations.
standard_prompt: An investigation reveals that attention-based neural networks exhibit superior performance in learning intuitively interpretable policies by leveraging feature representations across action and observation domains, facilitating efficient coordination tasks without requiring prior human interaction.
cot_prompt: An investigation into action feature networks shows that attention-based architectures outperform traditional methods by leveraging semantic relationships between actions and observations, leading to more interpretable and effective zero-shot coordination across different scenarios.
dsp_prompt: In investigating human-like action feature representations, researchers found that attention-based neural networks exhibit superior zero-shot coordination performance by capturing meaningful relationships between actions and observations, leading to more interpretable and effective policy learning.

titles: Why Clean Generalization and Robust Overfitting Both Happen in Adversarial Training
keywords: deep learning theory; adversarial robustness; adversarial training; clean generalization and robust overfitting
abstracts: Adversarial training is a standard method to train deep neural networks to be robust to adversarial perturbation. Similar to surprising $\textit{clean generalization}$ ability in the standard deep learning setting, neural networks trained by adversarial training also generalize well for $\textit{unseen clean data}$. However, in constrast with clean generalization, while adversarial training method is able to achieve low robust training error, there still exists a significant $\textit{robust generalization gap}$, which promotes us exploring what mechanism leads to both $\textit{clean generalization and robust overfitting (CGRO)}$ during learning process. In this paper, we provide a theoretical understanding of this puzzling phenomenon (CGRO) through $\textit{feature learning theory}$. Specifically, we prove that, under our theoretical framework (patch-structured dataset and one-hidden-layer CNN model) , a $\textit{three-stage phase transition}$ happens from adversarial training dynamics, and the network learner provably partially learns the true feature but exactly memorizes the spurious features from training-adversarial examples, which thereby results in CGRO phenomenon. Besides, for more general data assumption, we then show the efficiency of CGRO classifier from the perspective of $\textit{representation complexity}$. On the empirical side, we also verify our theoretical analysis about learning process in real-world vision dataset.
one_sentence_summary: We provide a theoretical understanding why clean generalization and robust overfitting both happen in adversarial training.
standard_prompt: Adversarial training's three-phase learning mechanism leads to partial true-feature learning and exact spurious-feature memorization, resulting in clean generalization and robust overfitting simultaneously.
cot_prompt: Adversarial training's three-phase learning process leads to partial feature learning and exact memorization of spurious features, resulting in clean generalization and robust overfitting simultaneously.
dsp_prompt: Adversarial training's three-stage phase transition causes neural networks to learn approximately the true feature space but exactly replicate the spurious patterns present in adversarial examples, leading to clean generalization and robust overfitting simultaneously.

titles: Zero-Shot Medical Image Artifact Reduction
keywords: zero shot; medical image; artifact reduction
abstracts: Medical images may contain various types of artifacts with different patterns and mixtures, which depend on many factors such as scan setting, machine condition, patients’ characteristics, surrounding environment, etc. However, existing deep learning based artifact reduction methods are restricted by their training set with specific predetermined artifact type and pattern. As such, they have limited clinical adoption. In this paper, we introduce a “Zero-Shot” medical image Artifact Reduction (ZSAR) framework, which leverages the power of deep learning but without using general pre-trained networks or any clean image reference. Specifically, we utilize the low internal visual entropy of an image and train a light-weight image-specific artifact reduction network to reduce artifacts in an image at test-time. We use Computed Tomography (CT) and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) as vehicles to show that ZSAR can reduce artifacts better than state-of-the-art both qualitatively and quantitatively, while using shorter execution time. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first deep learning framework that reduces artifacts in medical images without using a priori training set.
one_sentence_summary: We introduce a “Zero-Shot” medical image Artifact Reduction framework, which leverages the power of deep learning but without using general pre-trained networks or any clean image reference.
standard_prompt: A novel "Zero-Shot" framework, ZSAR, developed for reducing artifacts in medical CT and MRI scans through leveraging the intrinsic visual complexity of images, surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques by performing artifact reduction with minimal training requirements and comparable quality outcomes, achieving faster processing times compared to traditional approaches.
cot_prompt: A "Zero-Shot" medical image artifact reduction framework leveraging low-entropy features and lightweight neural networks achieves superior artifact reduction compared to state-of-the-art methods in CT and MRI scans, demonstrating its potential for practical application in reducing artifacts in medical imaging.
dsp_prompt: A novel "zero-shot" framework, Zero-Shot Medical Image Artifact Reduction (ZSAR), utilizes deep learning techniques trained specifically for reducing artifacts in CT and MRI scans, demonstrating superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods in terms of artifact reduction quality and efficiency, making it suitable for clinical applications in reducing artifacts in medical imaging without requiring a predefined dataset.

titles: A Boolean Task Algebra for Reinforcement Learning
keywords: Reinforcement Learning; Transfer; Composition; Lifelong; Multi-task; Deep Reinforcement learning
abstracts: We propose a framework for defining a Boolean algebra over the space of tasks. This allows us to formulate new tasks in terms of the negation, disjunction and conjunction of a set of base tasks. We then show that by learning goal-oriented value functions and restricting the transition dynamics of the tasks, an agent can solve these new tasks with no further learning. We prove that by composing these value functions in specific ways, we immediately recover the optimal policies for all tasks expressible under the Boolean algebra. We verify our approach in two domains, including a high-dimensional video game environment requiring function approximation, where an agent first learns a set of base skills, and then composes them to solve a super-exponential number of new tasks.
one_sentence_summary: We formalise the composition of tasks as a Boolean algebra and provide a method for producing the optimal value functions of the composed tasks with no further learning.
standard_prompt: A novel Boolean task algebra enables reinforcement learning agents to efficiently solve complex tasks by leveraging goal-oriented value functions and compositional strategies within a defined algebraic structure.
cot_prompt: A novel framework defines a Boolean algebra over task spaces, enabling reinforcement learning agents to learn goal-oriented value functions and compose these functions to solve a large class of new tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness through applications in complex environments like a high-dimensional video game.
dsp_prompt: A novel framework for reinforcement learning enables agents to learn and compose base tasks through Boolean operations, solving complex problems involving multiple objectives efficiently.

titles: Training Generative Adversarial Networks from Incomplete Observations using Factorised Discriminators
keywords: Adversarial Learning; Semi-supervised Learning; Image generation; Image segmentation; Missing Data
abstracts:
Generative adversarial networks (GANs) have shown great success in applications such as image generation and inpainting.
However, they typically require large datasets, which are often not available, especially in the context of prediction tasks such as image segmentation that require labels. Therefore, methods such as the CycleGAN use more easily available unlabelled data, but do not offer a way to leverage additional labelled data for improved performance. To address this shortcoming, we show how to factorise the joint data distribution into a set of lower-dimensional distributions along with their dependencies. This allows splitting the discriminator in a GAN into multiple "sub-discriminators" that can be independently trained from incomplete observations. Their outputs can be combined to estimate the density ratio between the joint real and the generator distribution, which enables training generators as in the original GAN framework. We apply our method to image generation, image segmentation and audio source separation, and obtain improved performance over a standard GAN when additional incomplete training examples are available. For the Cityscapes segmentation task in particular, our method also improves accuracy by an absolute 14.9% over CycleGAN while using only 25 additional paired examples.
one_sentence_summary: We decompose the discriminator in a GAN in a principled way so that each component can be independently trained on different parts of the input. The resulting "FactorGAN" can be used for semi-supervised learning and in missing data scenarios.
standard_prompt: Our approach factors the joint data distribution into sub-distributions and trains discriminators separately from incomplete observations, enabling effective GAN training even with limited labeled data, achieving superior performance in tasks like image generation and segmentation.
cot_prompt: Factorising the discriminators of generative adversarial networks into sub-discriminators trained from incomplete observations leads to improved performance through enhanced density estimation and accurate density ratio computation.
dsp_prompt: The authors propose a novel approach to train generative adversarial networks using factorized discriminators and incomplete observations, demonstrating improved performance across various tasks including image generation, segmentation, and audio source separation.

titles: PDE-Driven Spatiotemporal Disentanglement
keywords: disentanglement; spatiotemporal prediction; representation learning; dynamical systems; separation of variables
abstracts: A recent line of work in the machine learning community addresses the problem of predicting high-dimensional spatiotemporal phenomena by leveraging specific tools from the differential equations theory. Following this direction, we propose in this article a novel and general paradigm for this task based on a resolution method for partial differential equations: the separation of variables. This inspiration allows us to introduce a dynamical interpretation of spatiotemporal disentanglement. It induces a principled model based on learning disentangled spatial and temporal representations of a phenomenon to accurately predict future observations. We experimentally demonstrate the performance and broad applicability of our method against prior state-of-the-art models on physical and synthetic video datasets.
one_sentence_summary: We introduce a novel interpretation of spatiotemporal disentanglement, inducing a simple and performant disentangled prediction model.
standard_prompt: The proposed framework leverages the separation of variables technique inspired by partial differential equation resolution methods to achieve accurate prediction of high-dimensional spatiotemporal phenomena through a dynamic disentanglement approach, showcasing superior performance over existing models on both real-world and simulated data.
cot_prompt: A new framework for spatiotemporal disentanglement using partial differential equation solvers achieves accurate predictions through dynamic separable variable techniques, demonstrating superior performance over existing methods on both real-world and artificial data sets.
dsp_prompt: A novel dynamic framework using separation of variables resolves the challenge of spatiotemporal disentanglement through differential equation-based modeling, offering a principled approach for accurate high-dimensional predictions via learned spatial and temporal representations.

titles: Variadic Learning by Bayesian Nonparametric Deep Embedding
keywords: meta-learning; metric learning; bayesian nonparametrics; few-shot learning; deep learning
abstracts: Learning at small or large scales of data is addressed by two strong but divided frontiers: few-shot learning and standard supervised learning. Few-shot learning focuses on sample efficiency at small scale, while supervised learning focuses on accuracy at large scale. Ideally they could be reconciled for effective learning at any number of data points (shot) and number of classes (way). To span the full spectrum of shot and way, we frame the variadic learning regime of learning from any number of inputs. We approach variadic learning by meta-learning a novel multi-modal clustering model that connects bayesian nonparametrics and deep metric learning. Our bayesian nonparametric deep embedding (BANDE) method is optimized end-to-end with a single objective, and adaptively adjusts capacity to learn from variable amounts of supervision. We show that multi-modality is critical for learning complex classes such as Omniglot alphabets and carrying out unsupervised clustering. We explore variadic learning by measuring generalization across shot and way between meta-train and meta-test, show the first results for scaling from few-way, few-shot tasks to 1692-way Omniglot classification and 5k-shot CIFAR-10 classification, and find that nonparametric methods generalize better than parametric methods. On the standard few-shot learning benchmarks of Omniglot and mini-ImageNet, BANDE equals or improves on the state-of-the-art for semi-supervised classification.
one_sentence_summary: We address any-shot, any-way learning with multi-modal prototypes by connecting bayesian nonparametrics and deep metric learning
standard_prompt: A novel Bayesian nonparametric deep embedding framework called BANDE learns from varying amounts of supervision through adaptive clustering, achieving superior performance on Omniglot classification and showing significant improvements over traditional approaches on few-shot learning benchmarks.
cot_prompt: Bayesian nonparametric deep embedding learns effectively across different numbers of data points through multi-modal clustering, achieving superior performance in few-shot and unsupervised learning tasks compared to traditional parametric methods.
dsp_prompt: The novel multi-modal clustering model, BayesNonParametricEmbedding (BANDE), optimizes end-to-end through a single objective, dynamically adjusting its capacity based on varying amounts of supervision, significantly enhancing learning across different numbers of shots and ways by connecting Bayesian nonparametrics with deep metric learning, leading to improved performance in complex class recognition and unsupervised clustering, especially on tasks like Omniglot alphabets and beyond, showcasing superior generalization capabilities compared to traditional parametric methods.

titles: Hopper: Multi-hop Transformer for Spatiotemporal Reasoning
keywords: Multi-hop Reasoning; Object Permanence; Spatiotemporal Understanding; Video Recognition; Transformer
abstracts: This paper considers the problem of spatiotemporal object-centric reasoning in videos. Central to our approach is the notion of object permanence, i.e., the ability to reason about the location of objects as they move through the video while being occluded, contained or carried by other objects. Existing deep learning based approaches often suffer from spatiotemporal biases when applied to video reasoning problems. We propose Hopper, which uses a Multi-hop Transformer for reasoning object permanence in videos. Given a video and a localization query, Hopper reasons over image and object tracks to automatically hop over critical frames in an iterative fashion to predict the final position of the object of interest. We demonstrate the effectiveness of using a contrastive loss to reduce spatiotemporal biases. We evaluate over CATER dataset and find that Hopper achieves 73.2% Top-1 accuracy using just 1 FPS by hopping through just a few critical frames. We also demonstrate Hopper can perform long-term reasoning by building a CATER-h dataset that requires multi-step reasoning to localize objects of interest correctly.
one_sentence_summary: We propose Hopper, Multi-Hop Transformer, and CATER-h dataset to approach object-centric spatiotemporal reasoning in videos.
standard_prompt: Hopper, an innovative multi-hop transformer-based system, addresses spatiotemporal reasoning challenges in videos by leveraging object permanence and employs a contrastive loss to enhance performance, achieving high accuracy even with limited computational resources.
cot_prompt: Hopper, an innovative Multi-hop Transformer-based system, effectively addresses the challenge of spatiotemporal reasoning in videos by leveraging object permanence and achieving high accuracy in localizing moving objects with only 1 frame per second by strategically hopping across critical frames in sequential iterations.
dsp_prompt: Hopper, an innovative Multi-hop Transformer-based system, effectively addresses spatiotemporal reasoning challenges in videos by leveraging object permanence, achieving high accuracy (73.2%) with minimal computation costs by iteratively predicting object locations through critical frame hops.

titles: Accelerating Optimization using Neural Reparametrization
keywords: optimization; graph neural networks; neural reparameterization; neural tangent kernel
abstracts:
We tackle the problem of accelerating certain optimization problems related to steady states in ODE and energy minimization problems common in physics. 
We reparametrize the optimization variables as the output of a neural network. 
We then find the conditions under which this neural reparameterization could speed up convergence rates during gradient descent.
We find that to get the maximum speed up the neural network needs to be a special graph convolutional network (GCN) with its aggregation function constructed from the gradients of the loss function.
We show the utility of our method on two different optimization problems on graphs and point-clouds.
one_sentence_summary: We show that some optimization processes can be accelerated by making the parameters the output of a graph neural network with the graph arising from gradients of the loss.
standard_prompt: Reparameterizing optimization variables through a specialized GCN-based neural network accelerates convergence rates for both graph and point-cloud optimization tasks by leveraging the gradient structure to guide faster gradient descent updates.
cot_prompt: Our study explores how neural networks can optimize the convergence rate of gradient descent by reparameterizing the optimization process through specialized GCNs, demonstrating significant performance improvements on both graph and point-cloud optimization tasks.
dsp_prompt: We introduce neural reparameterization for optimizing functions by treating them as outputs of a neural network, finding that specialized GCNs can accelerate convergence through the neural tangent kernel framework.

titles: Many-Body Approximation for Tensors
keywords: Tensor decomposition; Energy based model; Tensor networks
abstracts: We propose a nonnegative tensor decomposition with focusing on the relationship between the modes of tensors. Traditional decomposition methods assume low-rankness in the representation, resulting in difficulties in global optimization and target rank selection. To address these problems, we present an alternative way to decompose tensors, a many-body approximation for tensors, based on an information geometric formulation. A tensor is treated via an energy-based model, where the tensor and its mode correspond to a probability distribution and a random variable, respectively, and many-body approximation is performed on it by taking the interaction between variables into account. Our model can be globally optimized in polynomial time in terms of the KL divergence minimization, which is empirically faster than low-rank approximations keeping comparable reconstruction error. Furthermore, we visualize interactions between modes as tensor networks and reveal a nontrivial relationship between many-body approximation and low-rank approximation.
one_sentence_summary: We formulate rank-free tensor decomposition focusing on interactions between tensor modes. We also illustrate the relationship between our model and existing low-rank approximation models using tensor networks.
standard_prompt: A novel many-body approximation technique for tensors is proposed, leveraging an information geometric framework and minimizing Kullback-Leibler divergence for efficient global optimization, demonstrating improved performance over traditional low-rank approaches through interactive tensor network visualizations.
cot_prompt: We introduce a many-body approximation method for tensors using an information geometric framework, demonstrating faster global optimization and better performance compared to traditional low-rank approximations through interactions between tensor modes.
dsp_prompt: We introduce a novel tensor decomposition method called "many-body approximation" using an energy-based model, demonstrating improved global optimization through interactions between tensor modes and revealing connections to traditional low-rank approximations.

titles: Unbiased Contrastive Divergence Algorithm for Training Energy-Based Latent Variable Models
keywords: energy model; restricted Boltzmann machine; contrastive divergence; unbiased Markov chain Monte Carlo; distribution coupling
abstracts: The contrastive divergence algorithm is a popular approach to training energy-based latent variable models, which has been widely used in many machine learning models such as the restricted Boltzmann machines and deep belief nets. Despite its empirical success, the contrastive divergence algorithm is also known to have biases that severely affect its convergence. In this article we propose an unbiased version of the contrastive divergence algorithm that completely removes its bias in stochastic gradient methods, based on recent advances on unbiased Markov chain Monte Carlo methods. Rigorous theoretical analysis is developed to justify the proposed algorithm, and numerical experiments show that it significantly improves the existing method. Our findings suggest that the unbiased contrastive divergence algorithm is a promising approach to training general energy-based latent variable models.
one_sentence_summary: We have developed a new training algorithm for energy-based latent variable models that completely removes the bias of contrastive divergence.
standard_prompt: The authors introduce an unbiased variant of the contrastive divergence algorithm by leveraging advancements in unbiased MCMC techniques, demonstrating improved performance over traditional methods through rigorous theoretical analysis and extensive numerical experimentation.
cot_prompt: The authors introduce an unbiased variant of the contrastive divergence algorithm, demonstrating significant improvements over the standard method through rigorous theoretical analysis and empirical testing.
dsp_prompt: The authors introduce an unbiased variant of the contrastive divergence algorithm for training energy-based latent variable models, demonstrating improved performance through rigorous theoretical analysis and numerical experiments.

titles: Exploiting Weight Redundancy in CNNs: Beyond Pruning and Quantization
keywords: Sparse tensor; tensor compaction; beyond pruning and quantization
abstracts:
Pruning and quantization are proven methods for improving the performance and storage efficiency of convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Pruning removes near-zero weights in tensors and masks weak connections between neurons in neighbouring layers. Quantization reduces the precision of weights by replacing them with numerically similar values that require less storage. In this paper we identify another form of redundancy in CNN weight tensors, in the form of repeated patterns of similar values. We observe that pruning and quantization both tend to drastically increase the number of repeated patterns in the weight tensors.
We investigate several compression schemes to take advantage of this structure in CNN weight data, including multiple forms of Huffman coding, and other approaches inspired by block sparse matrix formats. We evaluate our approach on several well-known CNNs and find that we can achieve compaction ratios of 1.4x to 3.1x in addition to the saving from pruning and quantization.
one_sentence_summary: In this paper, we propose an effective method and data structure to compact DNN models beyond pruning and quantization, by removing the repeated patterns of similar value in weight tensors.
standard_prompt: The authors explore exploiting weight redundancy in CNNs through compression techniques, achieving up to three times better compactness compared to traditional pruning and quantization alone.
cot_prompt: In this paper, we explore exploiting weight redundancy in CNNs through various compression techniques, achieving significant improvements over traditional pruning and quantization methods while maintaining competitive performance.
dsp_prompt: Exploiting repeated patterns in CNN weight tensors reveals new opportunities for efficient compression through novel techniques such as multiple forms of Huffman coding, demonstrating significant improvements over traditional pruning and quantization methods.

titles: Deep Learning of Determinantal Point Processes via Proper Spectral Sub-gradient
keywords: determinantal point processes; deep learning; optimization
abstracts: Determinantal point processes (DPPs) is an effective tool to deliver diversity on multiple machine learning and computer vision tasks. Under deep learning framework, DPP is typically optimized via approximation, which is not straightforward and has some conflict with diversity requirement. We note, however, there has been no deep learning paradigms to optimize DPP directly since it involves matrix inversion which may result in highly computational instability. This fact greatly hinders the wide use of DPP on some specific objectives where DPP serves as a term to measure the feature diversity. In this paper, we devise a simple but effective algorithm to address this issue to optimize DPP term directly expressed with L-ensemble in spectral domain over gram matrix, which is more flexible than learning on parametric kernels. By further taking into account some geometric constraints, our algorithm seeks to generate valid sub-gradients of DPP term in case when the DPP gram matrix is not invertible (no gradients exist in this case). In this sense, our algorithm can be easily incorporated with multiple deep learning tasks. Experiments show the effectiveness of our algorithm, indicating promising performance for practical learning problems.
one_sentence_summary: We proposed a specific back-propagation method via proper spectral sub-gradient to integrate determinantal point process to deep learning framework.
standard_prompt: Our novel approach leverages proper spectral sub-gradients to effectively optimize determinantal point processes within the deep learning paradigm, addressing the challenge of non-invertibility by incorporating geometric constraints, thereby enabling direct optimization and facilitating its integration across various deep learning applications.
cot_prompt: A novel deep learning method optimizes determinantal point processes by leveraging their Gram matrix through spectral sub-gradients, addressing computational stability issues and enabling integration into various machine learning tasks.
dsp_prompt: A novel method optimizes the determinantally constrained determinantal point process (DPP) term using L2 regularization and spectral subgradient descent, addressing stability issues and enhancing its applicability across diverse deep learning tasks.

titles: Learning Visual Representation with Synthetic Images and Topologically-defined Labels
keywords: topology; persistent homology; self-supervised learning; synthetic image
abstracts:
We propose a scheme for neural networks to learn visual representation with synthetic images and mathematically-defined labels that capture topological information. To verify that the model acquires a different visual representation than with the usual supervised learning with manually-defined labels, we show that the models pretrained with our scheme can be finetuned for image classification tasks to achieve an improved convergence compared to those trained from scratch. 
Convolutional neural networks, built upon iterative local operations, are good at learning local features of the image, such as texture, whereas they tend to pay less attention to larger structures. Our method provides a simple way to encourage the model to learn global features through a specifically designed task based on topology. Furthermore, our method requires no real images nor manual labels; hence it sheds light on some of the lately concerned topics in computer vision, such as the cost and the fairness in data collection and annotation.
one_sentence_summary: We propose a new type of pretext task for self-supervised learning with synthetic images and mathematically-defined labels to incentivise learning global topological features of images
standard_prompt: A novel approach uses synthetic images and topological labels to train convolutional neural networks, encouraging them to learn global features by leveraging their ability to process mathematical-topological relationships, demonstrating superior performance over traditional methods in both convergence speed and feature extraction capabilities.
cot_prompt: Our proposed scheme enables convolutional neural networks to learn both local and global features by encouraging them to capture topological information during training, demonstrating superior performance over traditional methods using synthetic images and automatically defined labels.
dsp_prompt: Our novel self-supervised learning approach, leveraging topological insights and synthetic imagery, enhances convolutional neural network (CNN) performance by encouraging global feature extraction, outperforming traditional methods in both training efficiency and accuracy across various image classification tasks.

titles: A Stochastic Derivative Free Optimization Method with Momentum
keywords: derivative-free optimization; stochastic optimization; heavy ball momentum; importance sampling
abstracts:
We consider the problem of unconstrained minimization of a smooth objective
function in $\mathbb{R}^d$ in setting where only function evaluations are possible. We propose and analyze stochastic zeroth-order method with heavy ball momentum. In particular, we propose, SMTP, a momentum version of the stochastic three-point method (STP) Bergou et al. (2019). We show new complexity results for non-convex, convex and strongly convex functions. We test our method on a collection of learning to continuous control tasks on several MuJoCo Todorov et al. (2012) environments with varying difficulty and compare against STP, other state-of-the-art derivative-free optimization algorithms and against policy gradient methods. SMTP significantly outperforms STP and all other methods that we considered in our numerical experiments. Our second contribution is SMTP with importance sampling which we call SMTP_IS. We provide convergence analysis of this method for non-convex, convex and strongly convex objectives.
one_sentence_summary: We develop and analyze a new derivative free optimization algorithm with momentum and importance sampling with applications to continuous control.
standard_prompt: We introduce SMTP, a momentum variant of STP for optimizing smooth functions via function evaluations alone, showing improved performance over STP across various learning scenarios compared to traditional derivative-based methods like policy gradients.
cot_prompt: We present SMTP, a momentum variant of the stochastic zeroth-order method STP, achieving significant performance improvements over existing derivative-free optimization techniques in learning environments, demonstrating its effectiveness across various difficulties.
dsp_prompt: A novel momentum-based stochastic optimization algorithm SMTP achieves significant performance improvements over existing methods in unconstrained minimization tasks, particularly excelling on complex learning-to-control problems across diverse MuJoCo environments.

titles: Examining Scaling and Transfer of Language Model Architectures for Machine Translation
keywords: language modeling; machine translation; prefixlm; causallm; model scaling; zero-shot transfer
abstracts: Natural language understanding and generation models follow one of the two dominant architectural paradigms: language models (LMs) that process concatenated sequences in a single stack of layers, and encoder-decoder models (EncDec) that utilize separate layer stacks for input and output processing. In machine translation, EncDec has long been the favoured approach, but with few studies investigating the performance of LMs. In this work, we thoroughly examine the role of several architectural design choices on the performance of LMs on bilingual, (massively) multilingual and zero-shot translation tasks, under systematic variations of data conditions and model sizes. Our results show that: (i) Different LMs have different scaling properties, where architectural differences often have a significant impact on model performance at small scales, but the performance gap narrows as the number of parameters increases, (ii) Several design choices, including causal masking and language-modeling objectives for the source sequence, have detrimental effects on translation quality, and (iii) When paired with full-visible masking for source sequences, LMs could perform on par with EncDec on supervised bilingual and multilingual translation tasks, but improve greatly on zero-shot directions by facilitating the reduction of off-target translations.
one_sentence_summary: We thoroughly explore language modeling for machine translation in terms of model architecture, model scaling and cross-lingual transfer
standard_prompt: This study investigates how various language model architectures scale and transfer their performance across different types of machine translation tasks, revealing varying strengths and weaknesses depending on factors like parameter size and specific design choices.
cot_prompt: In examining the architecture of language models for machine translation, researchers found that while LMs scale differently to increasing parameter size compared to Encoder-Decoder models, they can match or surpass Encoder-Decoder's performance when combined with specific techniques like causal masking and targeted language modeling.
dsp_prompt: Our study explores how various architectural choices in language models affect their performance in machine translation, showing that while LMs can outperform EncDec in some cases, they also face limitations when it comes to reducing off-target translations through full-visible masking.

titles: Revisiting Distributed Synchronous SGD
keywords: Optimization; Deep learning; Applications
abstracts: Distributed training of deep learning models on large-scale training data is typically conducted with asynchronous stochastic optimization to maximize the rate of updates, at the cost of additional noise introduced from asynchrony. In contrast, the synchronous approach is often thought to be impractical due to idle time wasted on waiting for straggling workers. We revisit these conventional beliefs in this paper, and examine the weaknesses of both approaches. We demonstrate that a third approach, synchronous optimization with backup workers, can avoid asynchronous noise while mitigating for the worst stragglers. Our approach is empirically validated and shown to converge faster and to better test accuracies.
one_sentence_summary: We proposed distributed synchronous stochastic optimization with backup workers, and show that it converge faster and to better test accuracies.
standard_prompt: Revisiting traditional distributed training methods reveals the strengths and weaknesses of asynchronous and synchronous approaches, highlighting the potential of a hybrid strategy involving backup workers to balance convergence speed and robustness against stragglers.
cot_prompt: Our study revisits the benefits and drawbacks of three distributed optimization methods—asynchronous stochastic gradient descent (SGD), synchronous SGD, and synchronous SGD with backup workers—and demonstrates that synchronous optimization with backup workers outperforms both by reducing asynchronous noise and effectively handling stragglers.
dsp_prompt: Revisiting traditional methods of distributed training in deep learning reveals that synchronous optimization combined with backup workers offers superior convergence speed and accuracy compared to either asynchronous or synchronous approaches, addressing their respective limitations.

titles: NCP-VAE: Variational Autoencoders with Noise Contrastive Priors
keywords: Variational Autoencoders; Noise Contrastive Estimation; Sampling
abstracts: Variational autoencoders (VAEs) are one of the powerful likelihood-based generative models with applications in various domains. However, they struggle to generate high-quality images, especially when samples are obtained from the prior without any tempering. One explanation for VAEs’ poor generative quality is the prior hole problem: the prior distribution fails to match the aggregate approximate posterior. Due to this mismatch, there exist areas in the latent space with high density under the prior that do not correspond to any encoded image. Samples from those areas are decoded to corrupted images. To tackle this issue, we propose an energy-based prior defined by the product of a base prior distribution and a reweighting factor, designed to bring the base closer to the aggregate posterior. We train the reweighting factor by noise contrastive estimation, and we generalize it to hierarchical VAEs with many latent variable groups. Our experiments confirm that the proposed noise contrastive priors improve the generative performance of state-of-the-art VAEs by a large margin on the MNIST, CIFAR-10, CelebA 64, and CelebA HQ 256 datasets.
one_sentence_summary: We address the prior hole problem in VAEs using an energy-based prior, trained with noise contrastive estimation.
standard_prompt: The noise contrastive priors introduced in the NCP-VAE framework address the prior hole problem in variational autoencoders, improving their generative performance through reweighted approximations to better match the aggregate posterior distribution across multiple latent variable groups.
cot_prompt: The authors introduce noise contrastive priors to address the prior hole problem in variational autoencoders, improving their generative capabilities through generalized noise contrastive estimation, demonstrating significant performance gains across multiple datasets.
dsp_prompt: Our novel noise contrastive priors address the prior hole problem in variational autoencoders, improving their generative capabilities across multiple datasets through effective reweighting.

titles: Quantized Reinforcement Learning (QuaRL)
keywords: Deep Reinforcement Learning; Quantization
abstracts: Recent work has shown that quantization can help reduce the memory, compute, and energy demands of deep neural networks without significantly harming their quality. However, whether these prior techniques, applied traditionally to image-based models, work with the same efficacy to the sequential decision making process in reinforcement learning remains an unanswered question. To address this void, we conduct the first comprehensive empirical study that quantifies the effects of quantization on various deep reinforcement learning policies with the intent to reduce their computational resource demands. We apply techniques such as post-training quantization and quantization aware training to a spectrum of reinforcement learning tasks (such as Pong, Breakout, BeamRider and more) and training algorithms (such as PPO, A2C, DDPG, and DQN). Across this spectrum of tasks and learning algorithms, we show that policies can be quantized to 6-8 bits of precision without loss of accuracy. Additionally, we show that certain tasks and reinforcement learning algorithms yield policies that are more difficult to quantize due to their effect of widening the models' distribution of weights and that quantization aware training consistently improves results over post-training quantization and oftentimes even over the full precision baseline. Finally, we demonstrate the real-world applications of quantization for reinforcement learning. We use half-precision training to train a Pong model 50 % faster, and we deploy a quantized reinforcement learning based navigation policy to an embedded system, achieving an 18x speedup and a 4x reduction in memory usage over an unquantized policy.
one_sentence_summary: We conduct 350+ experiments to show that RL models can be quantized to 6-8 bits without harming quality; show narrower weight distribution facilitates quantization; show quantization speeds training by 50% and inference by 18x.
standard_prompt: In a comprehensive study, QuaRL demonstrates that post-training quantization and quantization-aware training significantly improve the performance of deep reinforcement learning policies across diverse tasks and algorithms by reducing computational resources while maintaining or enhancing task-specific accuracy, including a 18x speedup and 4x reduction in memory usage using half-precision training on a Pong model.
cot_prompt: In a comprehensive study, researchers explore the effectiveness of quantization in reducing the computational requirements of deep reinforcement learning policies across various tasks and algorithms, demonstrating improved performance through both post-training and quantization-aware methods while identifying limitations for specific task types.
dsp_prompt: Quantizing deep reinforcement learning policies reduces computation requirements by up to 8 bits while improving performance across multiple tasks and algorithms through quantization-aware training, demonstrating significant benefits in terms of efficiency and scalability.

titles: Understanding and Bridging the Modality Gap for Speech Translation
keywords: neural machine translation; speech translation; modality gap
abstracts: How to achieve better end-to-end speech translation (ST) by leveraging (text) machine translation (MT) data? Among various existing techniques, multi-task learning is one of the effective ways to share knowledge between ST and MT, thus additional MT data can help to learn the source-to-target mapping. However, due to the differences between speech and text, there is always a gap between ST and MT. In this paper, we first aim to understand this modality gap from the target-side representation differences. We also link the modality gap to another well-known problem in neural machine translation: exposure bias, where the modality gap is relatively small during training except for some hard cases, but keeps increasing during inference due to the cascading effect. To address these problems, we propose the Cross-modal Regularization with Scheduled Sampling (Cress) method. Specifically, we regularize the output predictions of ST and MT, whose target-side contexts are derived by sampling between ground truth words and self-generated words with a varying probability. Furthermore, to handle the difficult cases with large modality gaps, we introduce token-level adaptive training to assign different training weights to target tokens according to the extent of the modality gap. Experiments and analysis show that our approach effectively bridges the modality gap, and achieves significant improvements over a strong baseline, which establishes new state-of-the-art results in all eight directions of the MuST-C dataset.
one_sentence_summary: We aim to understand the modality gap for speech translation and propose a simple yet effective Cross-modal Regularization with Scheduled Sampling (Cress) method to bridge this gap.
standard_prompt: Understanding and bridging the modality gap for speech translation involves addressing the difference in target-side representations between speech and text, particularly during inference, through cross-modal regularization methods like Cress, which adaptively assigns different training weights based on the modality gap's extent, leading to improved performance compared to traditional approaches.
cot_prompt: In this study, researchers explore how to bridge the modality gap in speech translation through multi-task learning combined with cross-modal regularization and scheduled sampling, addressing issues related to exposure bias and handling difficult cases with adaptive training, ultimately achieving significant improvements over current benchmarks.
dsp_prompt: In this study, we investigate the modality gap in speech translation using multi-task learning and cross-modal regularization methods, demonstrating improved performance through targeted adaptation and scheduled sampling strategies.

titles: Semi-parametric topological memory for navigation
keywords: deep learning; navigation; memory
abstracts: We introduce a new memory architecture for navigation in previously unseen environments, inspired by landmark-based navigation in animals. The proposed semi-parametric topological memory (SPTM) consists of a (non-parametric) graph with nodes corresponding to locations in the environment and a (parametric) deep network capable of retrieving nodes from the graph based on observations. The graph stores no metric information, only connectivity of locations corresponding to the nodes. We use SPTM as a planning module in a navigation system. Given only 5 minutes of footage of a previously unseen maze, an SPTM-based navigation agent can build a topological map of the environment and use it to confidently navigate towards goals. The average success rate of the SPTM agent in goal-directed navigation across test environments is higher than the best-performing baseline by a factor of three.
one_sentence_summary: We introduce a new memory architecture for navigation in previously unseen environments, inspired by landmark-based navigation in animals.
standard_prompt: A novel navigation strategy using a non-parametric graph and parametric neural networks achieves high accuracy in goal-directed navigation through partially observed environments, surpassing existing baselines significantly.
cot_prompt: A novel semi-parametric topological memory (SPTM) navigational system achieves high success rates in goal-directed navigation using only partial environmental data.
dsp_prompt: A novel semi-parametric topological memory (SPTM) architecture enables efficient goal-directed navigation in previously unseen environments through landmark-based reasoning and deep neural networks.

titles: Backpropagation at the Infinitesimal Inference Limit of Energy-Based Models: Unifying Predictive Coding, Equilibrium Propagation, and Contrastive Hebbian Learning
keywords: predictive coding; equilibrium propagation; contrastive hebbian learning; backprop; machine learning; computational neuroscience
abstracts: How the brain performs credit assignment is a fundamental unsolved problem in neuroscience. Many `biologically plausible' algorithms have been proposed, which compute gradients that approximate those computed by backpropagation (BP), and which operate in ways that more closely satisfy the constraints imposed by neural circuitry. Many such algorithms utilize the framework of energy-based models (EBMs), in which all free variables in the model are optimized to minimize a global energy function. However, in the literature, these algorithms exist in isolation and no unified theory exists linking them together. Here, we provide a comprehensive theory of the conditions under which EBMs can approximate BP, which lets us unify many of the BP approximation results in the literature (namely,  predictive coding, equilibrium propagation, and contrastive Hebbian learning) and demonstrate that their approximation to BP arises from a simple and general mathematical property of EBMs at free-phase equilibrium. This property can then be exploited in different ways with different energy functions, and these specific choices yield a family of BP-approximating algorithms, which both includes the known results in the literature and can be used to derive new ones.
one_sentence_summary: We unify and provide a single limit for many papers in the literature concerning when energy based models approximate backdrop, typically in the context of biologically plausible learning algorithms
standard_prompt: The authors propose a unified theory linking various "biologically plausible" algorithms for approximating backpropagation in energy-based models, showing how they converge to backpropagation when operating at the free-phase equilibrium state.
